root.label: Knowledge Graph-based Thought (KGT) Framework
root.summary: An innovative framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to improve the factual accuracy of pan-cancer question answering by utilizing verifiable information and reasoning on KG schemas.

llm_challenges.label: Challenges in LLM-based Biomedical QA
llm_challenges.summary: The primary obstacles preventing the real-world application of LLMs in biomedical sciences, specifically regarding accuracy.

factual_hallucinations.label: Factual Hallucinations
factual_hallucinations.summary: The generation of incorrect statements by LLMs due to gaps in internal knowledge or retrieval.

hallucination_cause_context.label: Lack of Contextual Information
hallucination_cause_context.summary: Inability of the LLM to comprehend questions because it lacks necessary contextual information. (Page 1)

hallucination_cause_knowledge.label: Insufficient Inherent Knowledge
hallucination_cause_knowledge.summary: The LLM lacks the required factual data to generate accurate answers. (Page 1)

hallucination_cause_recall.label: Incapacity to Recall Specific Facts
hallucination_cause_recall.summary: The failure of the model to retrieve specific, stored facts accurately during generation. (Page 1)

fine_tuning_limitations.label: Limitations of Fine-tuning
fine_tuning_limitations.summary: While fine-tuning (e.g., MedAlpaca, ChatDoctor, Med-PaLM) can reduce hallucinations, it introduces new systemic issues.

fine_tuning_cost.label: Training Expenses
fine_tuning_cost.summary: Fine-tuning LLMs on specialized medical data incurs considerable training costs. (Page 2)

catastrophic_forgetting.label: Catastrophic Forgetting
catastrophic_forgetting.summary: A phenomenon where a model forgets previously learned information due to parameter modifications during the acquisition of new tasks, deteriorating performance on prior tasks. (Page 2)

enhancement_strategies.label: LLM Enhancement Strategies
enhancement_strategies.summary: Existing methodologies used to improve LLM output accuracy without relying solely on basic fine-tuning.

prompt_engineering.label: Prompt Engineering
prompt_engineering.summary: The optimization of prompts to improve LLM effectiveness across complex tasks.

cot_prompting.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
cot_prompting.summary: Prompts that incorporate intermediate reasoning steps to enable complex reasoning capabilities. (Page 2)

ape_method.label: Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE)
ape_method.summary: An automatic prompt generation method designed to enhance LLM performance. (Page 2)

kgqa_methods.label: Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA)
kgqa_methods.summary: The use of structured repositories (KGs) to provide a dependable foundation for factual verification and precision in responses.

traditional_kgqa.label: Traditional KGQA
traditional_kgqa.summary: Methods existing before LLMs that focus on subgraph retrieval and structured queries.

subgraph_reasoning.label: Retrieval-plus-Reasoning Paradigm
subgraph_reasoning.summary: Retrieving a related subgraph to reduce search space, followed by multihop reasoning. (Page 2)

struct_gpt.summary: Navigates KGs by identifying pathways from a seed entity to a target answer entity. (Page 2)

schema_reasoning.summary: Unlike direct factual retrieval, KGT uses LLMs to infer entity information based on the schema of the knowledge graph to mitigate hallucinations. (Page 2)

kg_theory.label: Knowledge Graph Theory and Formalism
kg_theory.summary: The mathematical and structural definition of the knowledge graphs used in this work.

kg_formal_definition.label: KG Formal Definition
kg_formal_definition.summary: The KG is defined as K: E x R, storing entities (E) and relations (R).

fact_triplets.label: KG Triplets
fact_triplets.summary: KG is organized as a set of triplets {(e1, r, e2)} where r is a relation existing between pair of entities (e1, e2) in E x E.

kg_structural_elements.label: KG Structural Elements
kg_structural_elements.summary: Definitions of the paths and chains used for logical reasoning.

fact_relational_path.label: Relational Path
fact_relational_path.summary: A sequence of entity types (T) and the relation between them: {(t1, r, t2)} where (t1, t2) in T x T.

fact_relational_chain.label: Relational Chain
fact_relational_chain.summary: A specific set of relational triplets between actual entities: {(e1, r, e2)}.

fact_attributes.label: Attribute Information
fact_attributes.summary: Pairs (e, attr) where attr is an attribute associated with entity e, enhancing semantic richness and precision.

pcqa_dataset_scope.summary: The scale and thematic coverage of the PcQA dataset.

pcqa_tasks.label: Reasoning Task Categories (Table 2)
pcqa_tasks.summary: The four categories of logical reasoning problems implemented in PcQA.

fact_onehop_tail.label: Tail Entity Deduction
fact_onehop_tail.summary: Deduce tail entity T given head entity H1 and relation R1: H1 + R1 -> T?

fact_onehop_rel.label: Relation Inference
fact_onehop_rel.summary: Infer relation R given head entity H1 and tail entity T1: H1 + T1 -> R?

fact_multihop_rel_inf.label: Indirect Relation Inference
fact_multihop_rel_inf.summary: Deducing potential direct relations R? by navigating through indirect relations (R1, R2): H1 + T1 -> R1 + R2 -> R?

fact_multihop_ent_disc.label: Entity Discovery
fact_multihop_ent_disc.summary: Following a path from head entity H1 through intermediate relation R1 to find intermediate entity M, then applying R2 to find final tail T?: H1 + R1 -> M + R2 -> T?

task_intersection.label: Intersection Problems
task_intersection.summary: Taking the intersection of multiple relational chains.

fact_intersection_logic.label: Intersection Inference Process
fact_intersection_logic.summary: H1 + R1 -> T1 and H2 + R2 -> T2; the final answer is the intersection: T1 ∩ T2 -> T?

task_attribute.label: Attribute Problems
task_attribute.summary: Reasoning based on entity attributes (e.g., whether a drug is targeted therapy or a gene is oncogenic).

fact_attr_example.label: Attribute Query Example
fact_attr_example.summary: Example: 'What is the maximum age for recruitment of clinical trials for patients with meningioma?'

attribute_problems.label: Attribute Problems
attribute_problems.summary: A specific class of KGQA tasks focusing on entity attributes.

attr_def_1.label: Attribute Retrieval
attr_def_1.summary: The task of retrieving attributes of a known head entity H1 (represented as H1 -> PH1).

attr_def_2.label: Attribute Verification
attr_def_2.summary: Determining whether a tail entity T1, identified via head entity H1 and relation R1, satisfies specific attributes specified in a query.

kgt_workflow.label: KGT Workflow
kgt_workflow.summary: The end-to-end process of converting a natural language question into a reasoned answer using a Knowledge Graph.

question_analysis.label: Question Analysis
question_analysis.summary: The first stage of KGT where the natural language question is decomposed into manageable units.

key_info_extraction.label: Key Information Extraction
key_info_extraction.summary: The process of using an LLM to identify the head entity name (Hn), tail entity type (Tt), and tail entity attributes (Ta) from the question text (Q).

head_type_retrieval.label: Head Entity Type Retrieval
head_type_retrieval.summary: Utilizing a fixed Cypher format to query the Knowledge Graph for the head entity type (Ht) based on the extracted head entity name (Hn).

graph_schema_inference.label: Graph Schema-based Inference
graph_schema_inference.summary: The process of reasoning over the schema of the Knowledge Graph to find the most relevant relational path.

schema_graph_construction.label: Schema Graph Construction
schema_graph_construction.summary: Creation of an undirected graph G where nodes (N) are entity types (Et) and edges (P) are relations (R) derived from the SOKG.

candidate_path_search.label: Candidate Path Search
candidate_path_search.summary: Implementation of Breadth-First Search (BFS) to identify all shortest paths (SPs) connecting the head entity type (Ht) and tail entity type (Tt).

optimal_path_selection.label: Optimal Path (OP) Selection
optimal_path_selection.summary: The selection of the best relational path based on semantic similarity to the original question.

embedding_mapping.label: Embedding Mapping
embedding_mapping.summary: Textual information is mapped into a low-dimensional space resulting in N-dimensional real-value vectors.

similarity_calculation.label: Cosine Similarity Calculation
similarity_calculation.summary: Similarity between question Q and a shortest path SP is calculated using the dot product of vectors divided by the product of their magnitudes: Similarity(Q, SP) = (Q . SP) / (||Q|| * ||SP||).

op_maximization.label: OP Maximization
op_maximization.summary: The Optimal Path (OP) is defined as the path that maximizes the similarity score relative to the question: OP = max(Similarity(Q, SP)).

subgraph_construction.label: Subgraph Construction
subgraph_construction.summary: The stage where a specific portion of the KG is retrieved for final reasoning.

query_generation.label: Query Statement Generation
query_generation.summary: An LLM takes Ht, Hn, Tt, Ta, and OP as inputs to generate a formal query statement, typically in Cypher format.

subgraph_generation.label: Subgraph Generation
subgraph_generation.summary: The generated Cypher query is executed against the Knowledge Graph to produce a reasonable subgraph containing relevant relational chains and attributes.

final_inference.label: Final Inference
final_inference.summary: The conversion of KG data into a natural language answer.

subgraph_inference.label: Subgraph Inference
subgraph_inference.summary: Analysis of relational chains and attribute data to prune erroneous information and retain only correct chains relevant to the question.

nl_output_generation.label: Natural Language Output
nl_output_generation.summary: The LLM divides the pruned subgraph into multiple relational chains and generates a corresponding natural language sentence for each, synthesizing them into a final answer.

evaluation_methodology.summary: The metrics and datasets used to validate the KGT framework.

evaluation_metrics.label: Evaluation Metrics
evaluation_metrics.summary: Quantitative and qualitative measures for answer accuracy.

gpt4_eval.label: GPT-4 Evaluation
gpt4_eval.summary: Acts as a scoring bot to assign scores based on the semantic similarity in meaning between the generated and reference sentences.

bertscore_eval.label: BERTScore
bertscore_eval.summary: Evaluates semantic similarity using context-sensitive embeddings for a comprehensive assessment of LLM outputs.

rouge_eval.label: ROUGE
rouge_eval.summary: Evaluates the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) between generated and reference text to assess fluency and semantic preservation.

benchmark_dataset.summary: A newly proposed benchmark dataset specifically for biomedical KGQA used for all experiments in the study.

comparative_analysis.summary: Performance comparison of KGT against other models and baselines.

base_method.summary: A straightforward approach similar to KG-GPT but without the sentence segmentation step; uses an LLM to retrieve info via query and another to answer.

cot_icl_method.label: CoT&ICL
cot_icl_method.summary: The Base method enhanced with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and In-Context Learning (ICL).

def_icl.summary: The ability of a model to learn a task from examples provided in the prompt without parameter updates. (Page 10)

def_kgqa.label: KGQA (Knowledge Graph Question Answering)
def_kgqa.summary: The task of answering natural language questions using information retrieved from a knowledge graph. (Page 10)

def_rlhf.label: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback)
def_rlhf.summary: A method of aligning LLMs with human preferences. (Page 10)

def_sft.label: SFT (Supervised Fine-tuning)
def_sft.summary: The process of training a pre-trained model on a labeled dataset. (Page 10)

medical_llms.label: Medical Large Language Models (Med-LLMs)
medical_llms.summary: LLMs specifically adapted or trained for medical domains, with a significant focus on Chinese language medical capabilities.

chinese_medical_llms.label: Chinese Medical LLMs
chinese_medical_llms.summary: Specific models developed to handle the nuances of Chinese medical knowledge and patient interaction.

huatuo.label: Huatuo
huatuo.summary: A model based on tuning the Llama architecture with Chinese medical knowledge (Ref 10).

doctorglm.label: DoctorGLM
doctorglm.summary: A medical LLM focused on the efficiency of fine-tuning for Chinese medical expertise (Ref 11).

huatuogpt.label: HuatuoGPT
huatuogpt.summary: An effort toward taming language models to function specifically as doctors (Ref 12).

zhongjing.label: Zhongjing
zhongjing.summary: An LLM that enhances Chinese medical capabilities using expert feedback and real-world multi-turn dialogue (Ref 13).

chimed_gpt.label: ChiMed-GPT
chimed_gpt.summary: A Chinese medical LLM utilizing a full training regime and alignment with human preferences (Ref 14).

biomedical_llms.label: General Biomedical LLMs
biomedical_llms.summary: Models trained for diverse biomedical tasks beyond specific regional languages.

taiyi.label: Taiyi
taiyi.summary: A bilingual fine-tuned large language model designed for diverse biomedical tasks (Ref 43).

llm_training_optimization.label: LLM Training and Optimization
llm_training_optimization.summary: Techniques used to refine model behavior, prevent knowledge loss, and align output with human values.

alignment_techniques.label: Alignment Techniques
alignment_techniques.summary: Methods to ensure LLMs follow instructions and align with human preferences.

rlhf.label: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
rlhf.summary: Training models to follow instructions based on human-provided feedback (Ref 15).

direct_distillation.label: Direct Distillation (Zephyr)
direct_distillation.summary: A method for LM alignment through direct distillation (Ref 44).

continual_learning.label: Continual Learning
continual_learning.summary: The process of training models on new data without losing previously acquired knowledge.

learning_without_forgetting.label: Learning without Forgetting (LwF)
learning_without_forgetting.summary: A technical approach to prevent catastrophic forgetting during model updates (Ref 17).

prompt_engineering_reasoning.label: Prompt Engineering and Reasoning
prompt_engineering_reasoning.summary: Techniques used to elicit complex reasoning and better performance from LLMs through input design.

prompt_guidelines.label: Prompt Design Guidelines
prompt_guidelines.summary: Structured rules for prompt engineering, specifically applied to generative models (Ref 18, 20).

reasoning_strategies.label: Reasoning Strategies
reasoning_strategies.summary: Advanced prompting techniques to improve logical output.

cot.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting
cot.summary: A method that elicits reasoning by prompting the model to produce intermediate steps (Ref 19).

icl.label: In-Context Learning (ICL)
icl.summary: The ability of a model to learn tasks from a few examples provided within the prompt (Ref 41).

kg_kb_integration.label: Knowledge Graph (KG) and Knowledge Base (KB) Integration
kg_kb_integration.summary: Combining structured data (KGs/KBs) with the generative power of LLMs to reduce hallucinations and improve factuality.

kb_qa.label: Knowledge Base Question Answering (KBQA)
kb_qa.summary: Systems designed to answer natural language queries by retrieving data from structured knowledge bases.

open_domain_qa.label: Open Domain QA
open_domain_qa.summary: Question answering using early fusion of KBs and text (Ref 21) or iterative retrieval via PullNet (Ref 22).

multi_hop_qa.label: Multi-hop Question Answering
multi_hop_qa.summary: Complex QA requiring multiple steps of reasoning across a KG/KB (Ref 23, 25, 28).

subgraph_retrieval.label: Subgraph Retrieval
subgraph_retrieval.summary: Enhancing multi-hop KBQA by retrieving relevant subgraphs for reasoning (Ref 23).

graph_reasoning.label: Reasoning on Graphs
graph_reasoning.summary: Integrating LLMs with graph structures to perform deep, faithful, and interpretable reasoning.

structgpt.label: StructGPT
structgpt.summary: A general framework for LLMs to reason over structured data (Ref 28).

think_on_graph.label: Think-on-Graph
think_on_graph.summary: A framework for deep and responsible reasoning of LLMs on Knowledge Graphs (Ref 30).

reasoning_graphs.label: Faithful Graph Reasoning
reasoning_graphs.summary: Techniques for making LLM reasoning on graphs more interpretable and faithful (Ref 31).

factkg.label: FactKG
factkg.summary: A system for fact verification through reasoning on knowledge graphs (Ref 37).

specialized_medical_kgs.label: Specialized Medical Knowledge Graphs
specialized_medical_kgs.summary: Domain-specific graphs used to ground medical LLMs in scientific fact.

bio_kgqa_kgt.label: bioKGQA-KGT
bio_kgqa_kgt.summary: A KG-enhanced LLM framework specifically for pan-cancer question answering (Ref 33).

synlethdb.label: SynLethDB 2.0
synlethdb.summary: A web-based KG database focusing on synthetic lethality for anti-cancer drug discovery (Ref 34).

bertscore.label: BERTScore
bertscore.summary: A metric that evaluates text generation by leveraging BERT embeddings for semantic similarity (Ref 39).

rouge.label: ROUGE
rouge.summary: A package for the automatic evaluation of summaries based on n-gram overlap (Ref 40).

ehr_concept.label: Electronic Health Records (EHRs)
ehr_concept.summary: Digital versions of patients' paper charts, providing a holistic record of health, diagnoses, and treatment.

ehr_utility.label: EHR Utility
ehr_utility.summary: The role of EHRs in maintaining continuity of patient care.

ehr_utility_fact_1.label: Care Continuity
ehr_utility_fact_1.summary: EHRs provide a comprehensive account of patient health trajectory, including condition status, diagnoses, and treatment plans (p. 2).

ehr_challenges.label: EHR Challenges
ehr_challenges.summary: Problems associated with the current state of EHR documentation that lead to diagnostic errors.

complexity_issue.label: Narrative Complexity
complexity_issue.summary: Complex and verbose EHR narratives containing redundant information can overwhelm healthcare providers, increasing diagnostic inaccuracy risks (p. 1).

cognitive_shortcuts.label: Decisional Heuristics
cognitive_shortcuts.summary: Physicians may skip sections of lengthy notes and rely on decisional shortcuts (heuristics), which contribute to diagnostic errors (p. 2).

llm_concept.label: Large Language Models (LLMs)
llm_concept.summary: Advanced AI models used for diverse language tasks, applied here to automate diagnosis generation from progress notes.

llm_applications.label: Clinical LLM Applications
llm_applications.summary: The use of LLMs for tasks such as taking progress notes as input to generate summaries of active diagnoses (p. 2).

llm_risks.label: LLM Risks in Healthcare
llm_risks.summary: Critical concerns regarding the reliability of LLMs in medical settings.

hallucinations_fact.label: Information Hallucination
hallucinations_fact.summary: The potential for LLMs to produce misleading or hallucinated information (p. 2).

safety_fact.label: Patient Safety Risk
safety_fact.summary: Hallucinated information in a diagnostic context can lead to life-threatening events (p. 2).

llm_examples.label: Specific LLM Architectures
llm_examples.summary: Models utilized in diagnosis generation research.

t5_model.label: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (T5)
t5_model.summary: A language model developed by Google Research (p. 2).

gpt_model.label: Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)
gpt_model.summary: A language model developed by OpenAI (p. 2).

kg_concept.label: Medical Knowledge Graphs (KGs)
kg_concept.summary: Structured repositories of medical knowledge providing concept vocabularies and semantic relationships.

umls_system.label: Unified Medical Language System (UMLS)
umls_system.summary: A comprehensive medical knowledge repository developed by the National Library of Medicine in the US (p. 2).

umls_function.label: UMLS Functionality
umls_function.summary: Facilitates the integration, retrieval, and sharing of biomedical information through concept vocabularies and semantic relationships (p. 2).

umls_scale.label: UMLS Scale
umls_scale.summary: Contains approximately 4.5 million concepts and 15 million relations (p. 2).

dr_knows_system.label: DR.KNOWS (Diagnostic Reasoning Knowledge Graph System)
dr_knows_system.summary: A model integrating UMLS-based KGs with LLMs to improve diagnostic predictions by retrieving contextually relevant paths aligned with patient-specific information (p. 1).

dr_knows_architecture.label: DR.KNOWS Architecture
dr_knows_architecture.summary: The technical components used to identify and rank knowledge paths relevant to a patient's clinical context.

node_embedding_tech.label: Stack Graph Isomorphism Network
node_embedding_tech.summary: A network used within DR.KNOWS for node embedding (p. 1).

path_ranking_tech.label: Attention-based Path Ranker
path_ranking_tech.summary: A component used to identify and rank knowledge paths relevant to the patient's specific clinical context (p. 1).

dr_knows_evaluation.label: DR.KNOWS Evaluation and Results
dr_knows_evaluation.summary: The performance metrics and findings from real-world EHR dataset testing.

best_configuration.label: Optimal Configuration
best_configuration.summary: Prompt-based fine-tuning of T5 with DR.KNOWS knowledge paths achieved the highest ROUGE-L (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation–Longest Common Subsequence) and concept unique identifier F1-scores (p. 1).

human_evaluation.label: Clinical Safety Human Evaluation
human_evaluation.summary: Diagnostic rationales were found to align strongly with correct clinical reasoning, indicating improved abstraction and reasoning (p. 1).

dr_knows_limitations.label: System Limitations
dr_knows_limitations.summary: Identified constraints regarding data and generalizability.

kg_bias_fact.label: Knowledge Graph Bias
kg_bias_fact.summary: Potential biases within KG data exist; addressed by emphasizing case-specific path selection and proposing future bias-mitigation strategies (p. 1).

diagnostic_reasoning_concept.label: Clinical Diagnostic Reasoning
diagnostic_reasoning_concept.summary: The cognitive process used by clinicians to arrive at a diagnosis.

reasoning_process_steps.label: Steps of Diagnostic Decision-Making
reasoning_process_steps.summary: The process consists of: 1. Examination of patient data, 2. Retrieval of encapsulated medical knowledge, and 3. Formulation and testing of the diagnostic hypothesis (p. 2).

foundational_llms.label: Foundational LLMs
foundational_llms.summary: The pretrained language models used to generate diagnostic predictions based on medical narratives and KG paths.

chatgpt_model.label: ChatGPT
chatgpt_model.summary: A powerful LLM explored in a sandboxed version using zero-shot prompting for diagnosis generation. (p. 2)

grounding_mechanism.label: Knowledge Grounding
grounding_mechanism.summary: The process of feeding the top N case-specific knowledge paths into LLMs to reduce hallucinations and improve factual accuracy in domain-specific question-answering. (p. 2)

knowledge_graph_foundation.label: Knowledge Graph (KG) Foundation
knowledge_graph_foundation.summary: The structured medical knowledge source used to identify relevant diagnostic trajectories.

umls_specification.label: UMLS (Unified Medical Language System)
umls_specification.summary: A comprehensive, multilingual health terminology and the US national standard for EHRs and health information exchange. (p. 3)

cui_definition.label: Concept Unique Identifiers (CUIs)
cui_definition.summary: The nodes of the UMLS KG, which represent unique medical concepts. (p. 2)

snomed_ct.label: SNOMED CT
snomed_ct.summary: The Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine–Clinical Terms, the specific terminology system used for assigning identifiers to UMLS medical concepts. (p. 3)

reasoning_process.label: Diagnostic Reasoning Process
reasoning_process.summary: The method of navigating the KG to infer potential diagnoses from patient descriptions.

concept_extraction.label: Concept Extraction
concept_extraction.summary: The identification of starting concepts in the KG using extractors such as cTAKES (Clinical Text Analysis and Knowledge Extraction System) and QuickUMLS. (p. 3)

multihop_reasoning.label: Multihop Reasoning
multihop_reasoning.summary: A process where the system identifies direct neighbors of extracted concepts and performs subsequent hops (e.g., 2 hops) to find the top N most relevant nodes leading to a final diagnosis. (p. 3)

relation_optimization.label: Relation Optimization
relation_optimization.summary: The refinement of KG edges to maintain computational efficiency and retrieval accuracy. (p. 3)

relation_filtering_fact.label: Semantic Relation Filtering
relation_filtering_fact.summary: A board-certified physician reduced the 270 UMLS semantic relations to the 107 most relevant for diagnostics (e.g., including 'causative agent of' and excluding 'inverse isa'). (p. 3)

input_data_framework.label: Input Data Framework
input_data_framework.summary: The structure and sources of the clinical text used for diagnosis prediction.

soap_format.label: SOAP Format
soap_format.summary: The standard documentation format for daily progress notes used as the input for DR.KNOWS. (p. 3)

subjective_section.label: Subjective Section
subjective_section.summary: Contains the patient's self-reported symptoms, concerns, and medical history. (p. 3)

objective_section.label: Objective Section
objective_section.summary: Contains structural data collected by providers: vital signs (BP, heart rate), laboratory results, or physical examination findings. (p. 3)

assessment_section.label: Assessment Section
assessment_section.summary: A summary of the patient's overall condition, focusing on the most active problems and diagnoses for that day. (p. 3)

plan_section.label: Plan Section
plan_section.summary: Contains subsections outlining diagnoses or problems and their treatment plans; used as the ground truth for prediction. (p. 3)

datasets.label: Clinical Datasets
datasets.summary: The real-world hospital data used to train and evaluate the system.

probsum_dataset.label: ProbSum Dataset
probsum_dataset.summary: A subset of 1005 progress notes from MIMIC-III (deidentified ICU data from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, 2001-2012) with gold standard active diagnoses. (p. 4)

inhouse_ehr_dataset.label: In-house EHR Dataset
inhouse_ehr_dataset.summary: Data from adult patients (18+) admitted to the University of Wisconsin health system (2008-2021), covering ED, general medicine, and subspecialty wards. (p. 4)

evaluation_framework.label: Evaluation Framework
evaluation_framework.summary: The methodology used to validate the effectiveness and safety of the LLM-generated diagnoses.

human_evaluation_fact.label: Human Evaluation Framework
human_evaluation_fact.summary: The first human evaluation framework for LLM-generated diagnoses that adapts a survey instrument designed specifically to evaluate diagnostic safety. (p. 2)

data_layer.label: Data Sources and Preprocessing
data_layer.summary: The clinical datasets and knowledge bases used for training, ground truth establishment, and evaluation of the DR.KNOWS model.

umls_snomed.label: UMLS & SNOMED CT
umls_snomed.summary: The primary knowledge base providing the structured clinical vocabulary and semantic relations.

fact_t047.label: Semantic Type T047
fact_t047.summary: The semantic type 'T047 Disease and Syndromes' from the UMLS SNOMED CT vocabulary was used to extract concepts as ground truth data for training and evaluation. (Page 5)

fact_cui_definition.label: CUI (Concept Unique Identifier)
fact_cui_definition.summary: A unique combination of letters and numbers (e.g., C0243026) representing a specific concept in the UMLS; used interchangeably with 'node' in the graph model. (Page 5)

fact_kg_definition.label: UMLS Knowledge Graph (G)
fact_kg_definition.summary: Defined as G = VE based on SNOMED CT CUIs and semantic relations, where V is a set of CUIs and E is a set of semantic relations. (Page 5)

evaluation_datasets.label: Evaluation Datasets
evaluation_datasets.summary: Comparison between the in-house patient progress notes and the MIMIC-III dataset.

mimic_iii.label: MIMIC-III
mimic_iii.summary: Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III dataset.

fact_dataset_comparison.label: Dataset Statistical Differences
fact_dataset_comparison.summary: The in-house dataset had a greater number of input CUIs and extended CUI output compared to MIMIC-III, whereas MIMIC-III contained a wider range of abstractive concepts (concepts in gold standard diagnoses not found in input). (Page 5)

architecture_layer.label: Model Architecture
architecture_layer.summary: The multi-stage pipeline that retrieves, encodes, and ranks clinical knowledge paths to predict diagnoses.

node_representation.label: Contextualized Node Representation
node_representation.summary: The process of converting raw CUIs from input text into high-dimensional embeddings that capture both semantic and topological information.

sapbert_encoding.label: SapBERT Encoding
sapbert_encoding.summary: Self-alignment Pretrained Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers used to encode concept names concatenated with [SEP] tokens. (Page 5)

fact_sapbert_utility.label: SapBERT Utility
fact_sapbert_utility.summary: Chosen for its contrastive learning-based training which discriminates similar concepts and synonyms, showing state-of-the-art performance in entity linking. (Page 5)

sgin_encoding.label: Stack Graph Isomorphism Network (SGIN)
sgin_encoding.summary: A Graph Neural Network used to generate node embeddings by aggregating neighborhood information through graph convolution and nonlinearity. (Page 5)

fact_sgin_expressiveness.label: SGIN Expressive Power
fact_sgin_expressiveness.summary: Matches the expressive power of the Weisfeiler-Lehman graph isomorphism test, maximizing the ability to capture meaningful representations. (Page 5)

fact_sgin_stacking.label: SGIN Stacking Mechanism
fact_sgin_stacking.summary: Combines multiple GIN layers via matrix concatenation to compute the final node representation at layer K. (Page 5)

tfidf_weighting.label: CUI Weighting Scheme
tfidf_weighting.summary: A TF-IDF based weighting mechanism applied to assign higher weights to more relevant CUIs and semantic types. (Page 5)

fact_tfidf_logic.label: TF-IDF Logic
fact_tfidf_logic.summary: Designed to penalize less useful CUI types (e.g., temporal concepts like 'recent' C0332185) that are unlikely to lead to useful disease paths. Weights are multiplied by the concept representation hi. (Page 5)

path_reasoning.label: Path Reasoning and Ranking
path_reasoning.summary: The process of exploring n-hop subgraphs and scoring paths based on their alignment with patient-specific symptoms.

path_embedding_gen.label: Path Embedding Generation
path_embedding_gen.summary: Recursive aggregation of node embeddings and relation edges (encoded as one-hot embeddings) using a Feedforward Network (FFN). (Page 6)

fact_path_recursive_logic.label: Recursive Path Logic
fact_path_recursive_logic.summary: For the first hop, the path embedding pi equals the node embedding hi. For subsequent hops, it is recursively aggregated with new nodes and edges. (Page 6)

attention_mechanisms.label: Attention Mechanisms
attention_mechanisms.summary: Two mechanisms used to compute relevance scores (S) for paths relative to patient input text (hx) and input CUIs (hv).

multi_attn.label: Multihead Attention (MultiAttn)
multi_attn.summary: Explicitly captures relationships between input text, concept list, and the current path. (Page 6)

fact_multiattn_logic.label: MultiAttn Logic
fact_multiattn_logic.summary: Uses context relevancy matrix Hi and concept relevancy matrix Zi (utilizing concatenation, difference, and element-wise product) to represent logical relations like entailment, contradiction, and neutrality. (Page 6)

tri_attn.label: Trilinear Attention (TriAttn)
tri_attn.summary: Automatically learns complex relationships through the inner products of three matrices (hx, hv, pi). (Page 6)

fact_triattn_logic.label: TriAttn Logic
fact_triattn_logic.summary: Computes scores using a weight tensor Wabc summed over the dimensions of the input text, input CUIs, and path embeddings. (Page 6)

loss_functions.label: Loss Functions
loss_functions.summary: The objective function used to optimize the model, consisting of prediction and contrastive components.

pred_loss.label: CUI Prediction Loss (Lpred)
pred_loss.summary: Calculated using binary cross entropy to determine if the predicted node VN is present in the gold standard label Y. (Page 6)

cl_loss.label: Contrastive Learning Loss (LCL)
cl_loss.summary: Encourages the model to learn discriminative representations by comparing positive and negative samples. (Page 6)

learning_objective.label: Learning Objective and Training
learning_objective.summary: The mathematical and algorithmic approach used to train the DR.KNOWS model to identify relevant knowledge paths.

anchor_embedding.label: Anchor Embedding (Ai)
anchor_embedding.summary: The representation combining input text and concept information.

anchor_def.label: Anchor Embedding Definition
anchor_def.summary: Defined as Ai = hx ⊙ hv, where hx represents the input text and hv represents the concept representation.

similarity_measures.label: Cosine Similarity and Loss
similarity_measures.summary: The mechanism used to differentiate between correct and incorrect knowledge paths.

positive_feature.label: Positive Feature (fi+)
positive_feature.summary: Represents paths that correctly lead to the ground truth concept.

negative_feature.label: Negative Feature (fi-)
negative_feature.summary: Embodies paths that start from the source but culminate in an incorrect concept.

loss_mechanism.label: Loss Function Logic
loss_mechanism.summary: Measures loss when the similarity between an anchor and its positive feature is not significantly greater than the similarity between the anchor and a negative feature, given a specific margin for separation.

training_algorithm.label: Path Selection Algorithm
training_algorithm.summary: An iterative algorithm to optimize computational requirements.

algo_detail.label: Iterative Ranking
algo_detail.summary: The algorithm iteratively selects and ranks the most relevant paths to extend, avoiding the need to rank all n-hop paths within a single pass.

experimental_setup.label: Experimental Setup
experimental_setup.summary: The foundational models, datasets, and hardware infrastructure used in the study.

foundational_models.label: Foundational Models
foundational_models.summary: The language models used to evaluate the impact of DR.KNOWS.

t5_large.label: T5-Large
t5_large.summary: A model with 770 million parameters evaluated in fine-tuning scenarios.

t5_vanilla.label: Vanilla T5
t5_vanilla.summary: Foundational model used extensively in varied NLP tasks.

t5_flan.label: Flan-T5
t5_flan.summary: T5 variant fine-tuned using an instructional approach.

t5_clinical.label: Clinical-T5
t5_clinical.summary: T5 variant specifically trained on the MIMIC dataset.

gpt_3_5.label: GPT-3.5-Turbo
gpt_3_5.summary: A model with 154 billion parameters evaluated in zero-shot settings; serving as the framework for ChatGPT.

in_house_ehr.label: In-house EHR
in_house_ehr.summary: A private EHR dataset containing protected health information.

computing_environments.label: Computing Environments
computing_environments.summary: Hardware and network setups for data processing and model hosting.

google_cloud.label: Google Cloud Setup
google_cloud.summary: Used for MIMIC-III experiments; utilized 1 to 2 NVIDIA A100 40 GB GPUs and a server with 1 RTX 3090 Ti 24 GB GPU.

hospital_workstation.label: Hospital Research Workstation
hospital_workstation.summary: HIPAA-compliant network for in-house EHR data; equipped with a single NVIDIA V100 32 GB GPU.

local_cloud.label: Local Cloud Infrastructure
local_cloud.summary: Used to host a restricted version of ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo to ensure no data was sent to Microsoft or OpenAI.

input_constraints.label: Input Constraints and Preprocessing
input_constraints.summary: Handling token limits and content selection.

token_limits.label: Token Limits
token_limits.summary: T5 is limited to 512 tokens, whereas GPT can handle 4096 tokens.

content_selection.label: Content Selection
content_selection.summary: Input focused on 'subjective and assessment' sections of progress notes (physician evaluations) to fit T5's limit and avoid numerical 'objective' sections.

prompting_strategy.label: Prompting Strategy
prompting_strategy.summary: The engineering methods used to integrate graph knowledge into LLM prompts.

prompt_components.label: Prompt Components
prompt_components.summary: The three primary elements of the constructed prompt.

comp_format.label: Output Format
comp_format.summary: Specifies the format and template for the response.

comp_context.label: Context-Control Patterns
comp_context.summary: Linked directly to the input note and the output of DR.KNOWS.

betterprompt_method.label: BETTERPROMPT Technique
betterprompt_method.summary: A method for selecting optimal prompts based on language model likelihood.

bp_process.label: BETTERPROMPT Workflow
bp_process.summary: Manual task-specific prompts -> automatic paraphrasing (ChatGPT/back-translation) -> ranking by perplexity (averaged over sample inputs) -> selection of lowest perplexity prompts.

bp_personas.label: Prompt Persona Classification
bp_personas.summary: Subject matter prompts (developed by a critical care physician and medical informaticist) vs. non-subject matter prompts (developed by a computer scientist).

path_representations.label: Knowledge Path Representations
path_representations.summary: Methods of formatting graph paths as text.

rep_structural.label: Structural Representation
rep_structural.summary: Uses '→' to link source concepts, edges (relation names), and target concepts. This method showed superior performance.

rep_clause.label: Clause Representation
rep_clause.summary: Converts paths into clause-style text by joining source and target concepts with their relations.

intrinsic_evaluation.label: Intrinsic Evaluation (DR.KNOWS)
intrinsic_evaluation.summary: Evaluation of the graph model's ability to retrieve gold standard concepts.

gold_standard_def.label: Gold Standard CUI Set
gold_standard_def.summary: CUIs classified under semantic type T047 DISEASE AND SYNDROMES from the 'plan' section, with a maximum length of 2 hops between target and input CUIs.

intrinsic_metrics.label: Intrinsic Metrics
intrinsic_metrics.summary: Recall@N, Precision@N, and the F-score (harmonic mean of recall and precision).

extrinsic_evaluation.label: Extrinsic Evaluation (LLM)
extrinsic_evaluation.summary: Evaluation of the foundational models' performance on diagnosis prediction.

extrinsic_metrics.label: Extrinsic Metrics
extrinsic_metrics.summary: Recall, Precision, F-score, and ROUGE metrics (ROUGE-L based on longest common substring and ROUGE-2 based on bigram matching).

human_eval.label: Human Evaluation for Qualitative Analysis
human_eval.summary: A structured qualitative assessment framework designed to fill the gap in existing AI evaluation frameworks for diagnosis prediction, specifically assessing the 'reasoning' output of LLMs.

safer_dx_framework.label: Safer DX Instrument Framework
safer_dx_framework.summary: The foundational instrument upon which the human evaluation framework is based to provide a structured approach for assessing LLMs in diagnosis tasks.

safer_dx_fact.label: Framework Basis
safer_dx_fact.summary: The evaluation framework is based on the Safer DX Instrument [41] to gauge depth and accuracy of diagnostic reasoning processes. (p. 8)

eval_aspects.label: Evaluation Aspects
eval_aspects.summary: Five specific dimensions used to evaluate the model-generated reasoning section.

aspect_reading_comp.label: Reading Comprehension
aspect_reading_comp.summary: Captures whether the model understood the information contained within a progress note. (p. 8)

aspect_rationale.label: Rationale
aspect_rationale.summary: Captures the inclusion of incorrect reasoning steps within the model's output. (p. 8)

aspect_recall.label: Recall of Knowledge
aspect_recall.summary: Captures the hallucination of incorrect facts and the inclusion of irrelevant facts in the output. (p. 8)

aspect_omission.label: Omission of Diagnostic Reasoning
aspect_omission.summary: Captures instances where the model failed to support conclusions or provide evidence for a diagnostic choice. (p. 8)

aspect_abstraction.label: Abstraction and Effective Abstraction
aspect_abstraction.summary: Evaluates the amount of abstraction in the output to ascertain how knowledge paths influence output type and the model's ability to use abstraction. (p. 8)

scoring_methodology.label: Scoring Methodology
scoring_methodology.summary: The quantitative measurement system used for the qualitative aspects.

binary_scoring.label: Binary (Yes/No) Scoring
binary_scoring.summary: Omission, abstraction, and effective abstraction were formatted as yes or no questions. (p. 8)

likert_scoring.label: Likert Scale Scoring
likert_scoring.summary: Reading comprehension, rationale, and recall of knowledge were assessed on a 1-5 scale, where 1 indicates strong agreement with poor quality and 5 indicates strong disagreement (high quality). (p. 8)

eval_operational_process.label: Evaluation Operational Process
eval_operational_process.summary: The logistical execution of the human evaluation.

eval_personnel.label: Evaluation Personnel
eval_personnel.summary: The roles involved in the evaluation process.

medical_professionals_fact.label: Medical Professional Evaluators
medical_professionals_fact.summary: Two medical professionals were recruited to evaluate LLM outputs based on developed guidelines. (p. 8)

physician_advisors_fact.label: Physician Advisors
physician_advisors_fact.summary: Two senior board-certified clinical informatics physicians served as advisors, pilot testers, and trainers, using 5 sample cases to refine guidelines. (p. 8)

eval_tools.label: Evaluation Tools
eval_tools.summary: The software used for data collection.

redcap_fact.label: REDCap Web Application

fact_err_neglect.label: Failure to Leverage Paths

planner_agent.summary: Handles initial query analysis and task decomposition.

fact_planner_function.summary: Performs query disambiguation and decomposes complex queries into a structured plan P = {s1, s2, ..., sn}, where each si is a reasoning subtask, guided by CoT prompting with few-shot examples (Page 4).

step_definer_agent.summary: Translates abstract plan steps into executable queries.

retrieval_tool.summary: The module responsible for fetching external data.

qa_agent.label: QA Agent
qa_agent.summary: The synthesis engine for final answers.

fact_qa_agent_function.label: QA Agent Functionality
fact_qa_agent_function.summary: Synthesizes the final answer for each step using the filtered evidence and the specific subquery (Page 3/Figure 2).

architecture.summary: A modular system consisting of specialized agents and tools that are invoked dynamically based on a reasoning plan.

planner_fact_1.label: Planner Function
planner_fact_1.summary: Invoked once at the beginning of the process to generate a high-level reasoning plan for the query.

step_definer_fact_1.label: Grounding Mechanism
step_definer_fact_1.summary: Bridges high-level intent and low-level execution by grounding the subquery in current context and accumulated history Hi-1 = {(s1, a1), ..., (si-1, ai-1)}.

step_definer_fact_2.label: Output
step_definer_fact_2.summary: Produces a detailed subquery for each step si to enable precise and relevant document retrieval.

retrieval_fact_1.label: Technical Implementation
retrieval_fact_1.summary: Built on FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) for scalability.

retrieval_fact_2.label: Preprocessing
retrieval_fact_2.summary: Texts are preprocessed into chunks and embedded using a pretrained encoder.

retrieval_fact_3.label: Inference Process
retrieval_fact_3.summary: The subquery is encoded into a vector and matched against the index via inner product.

retrieval_fact_4.label: Output
retrieval_fact_4.summary: Returns the top-k relevant passages for dynamic, on-demand knowledge augmentation.

extractor_fact_1.label: Filtering Logic
extractor_fact_1.summary: Selects and aggregates specific sentences or spans directly aligned with the current subquery instead of appending entire chunks.

extractor_fact_2.label: Noise Mitigation
extractor_fact_2.summary: Filters out redundant/irrelevant content and mitigates the 'lost-in-the-middle' issue (Liu et al., 2024a).

extractor_fact_3.label: Evidence Aggregation
extractor_fact_3.summary: Combines complementary information from multiple sources into a concise evidence set for the QA agent.

extractor_fact_4.label: Context Management
extractor_fact_4.summary: Summarizes relevant content at each step to avoid context overflow in multi-hop queries, passing only the step-level query and summary forward.

qa_fact_1.label: Synthesis Method
qa_fact_1.summary: Uses in-context learning to synthesize an answer ai based on the step-specific query and filtered evidence.

qa_fact_2.label: Output Flow
qa_fact_2.summary: Produces a response ai for each step si; once all steps are complete, the final answer is assembled and returned to the user.

workflow.label: Operational Workflow
workflow.summary: The logic governing agent orchestration and state management.

workflow_fact_1.label: Dynamic Invocation
workflow_fact_1.summary: Orchestrates agents on demand based on the reasoning plan rather than using a fixed pipeline.

workflow_fact_2.label: Execution Sequence
workflow_fact_2.summary: Planner (once) -> [Step Definer -> Retrieval Tool -> Extractor Agent -> QA Agent] (repeated for each step si).

workflow_fact_3.label: State Maintenance
workflow_fact_3.summary: Maintains state throughout the reasoning trajectory, allowing each agent to condition on the evolving context (answer ai is added to history Hi).

kgrag_code_fact.label: KG-RAG Code and Data
kgrag_code_fact.summary: Code and biomedical benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/BaranziniLab/KG_RAG (Page 1).

entity_retrieval.summary: The process of identifying and retrieving disease concepts using vector embeddings.

chromadb_storage.label: Chroma Vector Database
chromadb_storage.summary: The storage system used for disease concept embeddings.

similarity_selection.summary: Disease concepts with the highest vector similarity to the extracted entity are selected for context retrieval.

fallback_mechanism.summary: If zero-shot approach fails to identify a disease entity, five disease concepts with the most significant semantic similarity to the entire input prompt are selected from the vector database.

spoke_composition.summary: Technical scale and structure of the SPOKE KG.

spoke_source_fact.summary: Assembled by integrating information from 41 different biomedical databases.

spoke_nature.summary: Vast majority of SPOKE is composed of curated information from systematic experimental measurements, specifically avoiding reliance on text mining from literature.

transformation_process.label: Graph-to-Natural Language Transformation
transformation_process.summary: The process of converting structured graph data from SPOKE into a format compatible with LLMs.

context_extraction.label: Context Extraction
context_extraction.summary: Fetching neighbor nodes associated with a disease node via API with specific quality filters.

api_endpoint_fact.label: API Endpoint
api_endpoint_fact.summary: Uses SPOKE's REST-API service, specifically the '/api/v1/neighborhood/' endpoint.

filter_treatments_fact.label: Treatment Association Filter
filter_treatments_fact.summary: Restricts treatment associations to those with clinical phase >= 3.

predicate_transformation.label: Predicate to Natural Language Transformation
predicate_transformation.summary: The systematic conversion of SPOKE predicates into English strings.

predicate_schema_fact.summary: Schema: UpperCase(predicateName)_<upperCase(firstLetter(subjectType)), lowerCase(firstLetter(predicateName)), upperCase(firstLetter(objectType))>. Example: 'ASSOCIATES_DaG' connects Disease (D) nodes with Gene (G) nodes via predicate 'ASSOCIATES'.

transformation_rule_fact.label: Transformation Rule
transformation_rule_fact.summary: The rule (S, P, O) -> Subject lowerCase(predicateName) Object is applied to create English sentences.

transformation_example_fact.label: Transformation Example
transformation_example_fact.summary: (disease hypertension, ASSOCIATES_DaG, gene VHL) transforms to 'disease hypertension associates Gene VHL'.

provenance_incorporation.label: Provenance and Evidence Incorporation
provenance_incorporation.summary: Adding metadata and statistical evidence to the extracted triples.

provenance_fact.label: Provenance Extraction
provenance_fact.summary: Extracts provenance information given as edge attributes.

evidence_flag_fact.label: Evidence Incorporation
evidence_flag_fact.summary: The '-e' flag in the KG-RAG script includes supporting evidence such as P-values or z-scores in the output.

pruning_embedding_fact.label: Pruning Embedding
pruning_embedding_fact.summary: Input prompt and all extracted contextual associations are embedded into the same vector space (Context Latent space) using a sentence transformer model.

pruning_condition_1.label: Similarity Distribution Condition
pruning_condition_1.summary: Prompt-context cosine similarity must be greater than the 75th percentile of the similarity distribution for the chosen disease node.

pruning_condition_2.summary: Prompt-context cosine similarity must have a minimum value of 0.5.

llm_integration.summary: The final stage where the enriched prompt (input prompt + prompt-aware context) is processed by an LLM.

evaluation_validation.summary: The empirical process of optimizing the KG-RAG framework.

hyperparams_concept.summary: Parameters tuned to balance context and accuracy.

cypher_rag.label: Cypher-RAG
cypher_rag.summary: A technique for retrieving context from a Neo4j graph database by generating Cypher queries using an LLM.

cypher_rag_mechanism.label: Cypher-RAG Mechanism
cypher_rag_mechanism.summary: The operational flow of transforming natural language into graph queries.

cypher_step_1.label: Schema Embedding
cypher_step_1.summary: The graph schema is explicitly embedded into the input prompt to guide the LLM.

cypher_step_2.label: Query Generation
cypher_step_2.summary: The LLM generates a structured Cypher query based on the embedded schema.

cypher_step_3.label: Context Retrieval
cypher_step_3.summary: The generated Cypher query is executed against the Neo4j database to retrieve information used as context for the final response.

cypher_langchain.label: LangChain Integration
cypher_langchain.summary: Cypher-RAG is integrated into the LangChain python library via the GraphCypherQAChain class.

cypher_rag_analysis.label: Cypher-RAG Analysis
cypher_rag_analysis.summary: Evaluation of the advantages and limitations of the Cypher-RAG approach.

cypher_adv.label: Advantage: Natural Language Interface
cypher_adv.summary: Allows creation of Cypher queries from natural language, removing the requirement for users to know Cypher syntax.

cypher_lim_tokens.label: Limitation: Token Usage
cypher_lim_tokens.summary: Explicit schema embedding restricts input token space and increases token usage; complex schemas require LLMs with longer context windows.

cypher_lim_sensitivity.label: Limitation: Prompt Sensitivity
cypher_lim_sensitivity.summary: The method is sensitive to prompt formulation; slight perturbations can lead to retrieval failure.

full_text_index.label: Full-text Indexing
full_text_index.summary: A method for node matching in Neo4j using semantic interpretation of string data.

lucene_power.label: Apache Lucene Integration
lucene_power.summary: Neo4j full-text indexing is powered by the Apache Lucene indexing and search library.

spoke_indexing.label: SPOKE Indexing Parameters
spoke_indexing.summary: In the SPOKE graph, all nodes are full-text indexed on their 'name' and 'identifier' properties.

full_text_process.label: Full-text Matching Process
full_text_process.summary: The mechanism used to map user queries to graph nodes.

full_text_semantic.label: Semantic Interpretation
full_text_semantic.summary: Stores individual words within string properties, enabling content-based matching beyond exact or substring matching.

full_text_scoring.label: Proximity Scoring
full_text_scoring.summary: The procedure compares the query against indexed disease names to yield a proximity score; the node with the highest score is selected.

kg_rag_pipeline.label: KG-RAG Pipeline Steps
kg_rag_pipeline.summary: The multi-step process for generating an answer using KG-RAG.

step_1.label: Entity Recognition
step_1.summary: Step i: Identify entities from the user prompt.

step_2.label: Concept Extraction
step_2.summary: Step ii: Extract biomedical concepts from the SPOKE graph.

step_3.label: Concept Embedding
step_3.summary: Step iii: Perform embedding of the extracted concepts.

step_5.label: Natural Language Conversion
step_5.summary: Step v: Convert the graph context into natural language.

step_6.label: Prompt Assembly
step_6.summary: Step vi: Assemble the final prompt for the LLM.

step_7.label: Answer Generation
step_7.summary: Step vii: Generate the final answer using the LLM.

kg_rag_hyperparameters.label: KG-RAG Hyperparameters
kg_rag_hyperparameters.summary: Key settings used to optimize context retrieval.

context_volume.label: Context Volume
context_volume.summary: Defines the upper limit on the number of graph connections permitted to flow from the KG to the LLM. Optimized value: 150 (100 for True/False questions).

embedding_model.label: Context Embedding Model
embedding_model.summary: Extracts graph context showing semantic similarity to the user prompt. PubMedBert was selected over MiniLM due to higher performance.

pubmedbert_perf.label: PubMedBert Performance
pubmedbert_perf.summary: Mean Jaccard similarity: 0.67 for single disease entities (10% higher than MiniLM) and 0.4 for two disease entities (8.1% higher than MiniLM).

minilm_perf.label: MiniLM Performance
minilm_perf.summary: Mean Jaccard similarity: 0.61 for single disease entities and 0.37 for two disease entities.

kg_rag_comparison.label: Comparative Analysis
kg_rag_comparison.summary: Evaluation of KG-RAG against Cypher-RAG and Full-text index methods.

comp_accuracy.label: Retrieval Accuracy
comp_accuracy.summary: KG-RAG achieved 97% accuracy, compared to 75% for Cypher-RAG and 61% for Full-text index.

comp_robustness.label: Retrieval Robustness
comp_robustness.summary: Against lowercase entity perturbation: KG-RAG maintained 97% accuracy; Full-text index dropped slightly (61% to 58%); Cypher-RAG dropped to 0% due to precise matching requirements.

comp_tokens.label: Token Usage
comp_tokens.summary: KG-RAG is most cost-effective with 3693 tokens on average, compared to 8006 for Cypher-RAG and 10590 for Full-text index.

comp_provenance.label: Provenance Information
comp_provenance.summary: Only KG-RAG was capable of extracting provenance information linked to assertions from the context.

framework_characteristics.label: Framework Characteristics
framework_characteristics.summary: The technical attributes and efficiency metrics of the KG-RAG system.

token_efficiency.label: Token Efficiency
token_efficiency.summary: The ability of KG-RAG to reduce the number of tokens used in prompts compared to other RAG methods.

fact_token_reduction_cypher.label: Token Reduction vs Cypher-RAG
fact_token_reduction_cypher.summary: KG-RAG represents a 53.9% reduction in token usage compared to Cypher-RAG. (Page 8)

fact_token_reduction_fulltext.label: Token Reduction vs Full-text Index
fact_token_reduction_fulltext.summary: KG-RAG represents a 65.1% reduction in token usage compared to full-text indexing. (Page 8)

fact_schema_requirement.label: Minimal Schema Requirement
fact_schema_requirement.summary: Unlike Cypher-RAG, which incorporates the entire graph schema into the prompt, KG-RAG requires minimal graph schema, eliminating the need to include it in the prompt. (Page 8)

knowledge_fusion.label: Knowledge Fusion
knowledge_fusion.summary: The mechanism by which KG-RAG improves LLM accuracy.

fact_fusion_mechanism.label: Explicit and Implicit Fusion
fact_fusion_mechanism.summary: Performance improvements are hypothesized to arise from the fusion of explicit knowledge from the Knowledge Graph (KG) and implicit knowledge from the LLM, providing domain-specific ground truth at a fine-grained resolution. (Page 8)

resource_accessibility.label: Resource Accessibility
resource_accessibility.summary: The impact of KG-RAG on the usability of large biomedical datasets.

fact_democratization_spoke.label: SPOKE Democratization
fact_democratization_spoke.summary: KG-RAG enables researchers and clinicians to leverage the SPOKE knowledge graph (containing over 40 million nodes) via natural language without requiring specialized graph query language skills. (Page 8)

fact_context_window_requirement.label: Reduced Context Window Requirement
fact_context_window_requirement.summary: Because it is more efficient in token utilization, KG-RAG can operate with LLMs that have relatively smaller context window sizes compared to Cypher-RAG or full-text indexing. (Page 8)

performance_benchmarking.label: Performance Benchmarking
performance_benchmarking.summary: Evaluation of KG-RAG across different LLMs and dataset types.

benchmark_datasets.label: Benchmark Datasets
benchmark_datasets.summary: The human-curated datasets used to validate the framework.

fact_dataset_types.label: True/False and MCQ Datasets
fact_dataset_types.summary: Performance was measured using domain-expert reviewed True/False and Multiple Choice Question (MCQ) datasets. (Page 8)

model_results.label: Model Results
model_results.summary: Comparative performance metrics for specific LLM architectures.

llama2_performance.label: Llama-2-13b Performance
llama2_performance.summary: The impact of KG-RAG on open-source model capabilities.

fact_llama2_mcq_boost.label: MCQ Accuracy Increase

gpt_comparison.label: GPT Model Comparison
gpt_comparison.summary: Relative performance of GPT-3.5-Turbo vs GPT-4 within the KG-RAG framework.

comparative_methodologies.label: Comparative Methodologies
comparative_methodologies.summary: Other retrieval methods compared against KG-RAG.

cypher_rag_details.summary: A RAG approach utilizing the Cypher query language.

fact_lucene_usage.summary: The study compared KG-RAG against traditional full-text indexing using Apache Lucene. (Page 8)
