fact_domain_versatility.label: Domain Versatility
fact_domain_versatility.summary: REIC demonstrates effectiveness in both in-domain and out-of-domain scenarios. (Page 1)

related_methodologies.label: Related Methodologies
related_methodologies.summary: Evolution of intent classification techniques from traditional to modern LLM-based approaches.

early_classifiers.label: Early Classifiers
early_classifiers.summary: Foundational methods relying on simpler statistical or recurrent architectures.

fact_svm_vs_lstm.label: SVM with Hierarchical Taxonomy
fact_svm_vs_lstm.summary: Research indicates that a simple SVM with a hierarchical label taxonomy can outperform deeper LSTM models for multi-domain intent datasets. (Page 2)

transformer_classifiers.label: Transformer-based Classifiers
transformer_classifiers.summary: Models utilizing self-attention and multi-task learning for enhanced understanding.

fact_joint_intent_mapping.label: Joint Intent Mapping
fact_joint_intent_mapping.summary: The use of models that simultaneously classify high-level intent and map queries to fine-grained product categories. (Page 2)

fact_memory_networks.label: Memory Networks for Scale
fact_memory_networks.summary: Utilization of slowly updated text encoders and global/local memory networks to prevent catastrophic forgetting and parameter explosion. (Page 2)

modern_llm_approaches.label: Modern LLM Approaches
modern_llm_approaches.summary: Current trends utilizing pre-trained large language models and prompting.

fact_zero_shot_xlm.label: Zero-Shot XLM Integration
fact_zero_shot_xlm.summary: Integration of fine-tuned XLM-based classifiers with LLMs to treat multi-turn intent understanding as a zero-shot task. (Page 2)

fact_retrieval_prompting.label: Retrieval-based Prompting
fact_retrieval_prompting.summary: Exploration of retrieval-based methods for intent classification and slot filling in few-shot settings. (Page 2)

icl_mechanism.label: In-Context Learning (ICL)
icl_mechanism.summary: The technique of providing a few examples in the prompt to guide the LLM's output.

icl_fine_tuning_stage.label: ICL in Fine-Tuning
icl_fine_tuning_stage.summary: Application of ICL during the data generation phase of LLM fine-tuning. (Page 2)

icl_inference_stage.label: ICL at Inference-Time
icl_inference_stage.summary: Application of ICL at inference-time using an intent candidate retriever to improve accuracy. (Page 2)

intent_classification_fundamentals.label: Intent Classification Fundamentals
intent_classification_fundamentals.summary: The theoretical basis of mapping customer queries to pre-defined intents, contrasting flat and hierarchical approaches.

flat_classification.label: Flat Classification
flat_classification.summary: A multiclass text classification approach that assumes independence among intent labels.

flat_math_def.label: Flat Classification Formal Definition
flat_math_def.summary: Given a customer query q in Q, the goal is to map it to one of k pre-defined intents t in T using a model M such that predicted intent t_hat = arg max P(t | q; theta), where theta represents model parameters. (Section 3)

flat_scalability_challenge.label: Scalability Challenge
flat_scalability_challenge.summary: A large number of labels in flat classification makes the system inefficient and difficult to maintain at industry scale. (Section 3)

flat_correlation_challenge.label: Label Correlation Challenge
flat_correlation_challenge.summary: Flat classification treats related intents (e.g., 'Order Issue' vs 'Track Order') independently, ignoring useful hierarchical structure. (Section 3)

hierarchical_classification.label: Hierarchical Intent Classification
hierarchical_classification.summary: An approach where queries are classified progressively from general to specific intents to improve efficiency and accuracy.

hierarchical_benefits.label: Hierarchical Benefits
hierarchical_benefits.summary: By creating a hierarchical ontology, the number of intents per classification head is reduced (e.g., from 103 flattened labels to less than 50 per head), making it more manageable for LLMs. (Section 3)

business_verticals.label: Business Verticals
business_verticals.summary: The organization of intents across different business domains.

first_party_business.label: First-Party (1P) Business
first_party_business.summary: Vertical dealing with customer contacts regarding first-party digital or device issues. (Section 3)

third_party_business.label: Third-Party (3P) Business
third_party_business.summary: Vertical dealing with customer contacts about third-party physical retail orders or consumer accounts. (Section 3)

reic_methodology.label: REIC Methodology
reic_methodology.summary: The three-component technical pipeline consisting of Index Construction, Candidate Retrieval, and Intent Probability Calculation.

index_construction.label: Index Construction
index_construction.summary: The process of creating a searchable database of query-intent pairs.

index_composition.label: Index Composition
index_composition.summary: A dense vector index containing (query, intent) pairs sourced from a held-out annotated dataset, where intent labels follow a hierarchical structure with d dimensions of domain knowledge. (Section 4)

index_encoding.label: Index Encoding
index_encoding.summary: Queries are encoded using a pre-trained sentence transformer model to generate dense vector representations. (Section 4)

candidate_retrieval.label: Candidate Retrieval
candidate_retrieval.summary: The mechanism for identifying the most relevant examples for a given query.

retrieval_process.label: Retrieval Process
retrieval_process.summary: A new query q is encoded into vector v_q; an approximate nearest neighbor search is then performed to retrieve the top-k most similar (query, intent) pairs, denoted as set E. (Section 4)

similarity_metric.label: Cosine Distance Similarity
similarity_metric.summary: Similarity is computed as sim(q, qi) = (v_q dot v_i) / (||v_q|| * ||v_i||), where v_i is the vector encoding of the i-th indexed query. (Section 4)

intent_probability_calculation.label: Intent Probability Calculation
intent_probability_calculation.summary: The use of a fine-tuned LLM to rank retrieved candidates via constrained decoding.

constrained_decoding.label: Constrained Decoding
constrained_decoding.summary: A technique to prevent LLM hallucinations (generating intents outside the candidate list) by calculating the probability of each retrieved intent t_j in set E. (Section 4)

probability_formula.label: Probability Computation
probability_formula.summary: The probability for intent t_j is calculated as M(P, q, E)t_j = exp(sum(LogSoftmax(L_tj)) / s_j), where L_tj are logits from the forward pass and s_j is the intent sequence length. (Section 4)

inference_mechanism.label: Inference Mechanism
inference_mechanism.summary: Instead of auto-regressive decoding, REIC performs one model forward-pass with batch size k for top-k candidates to obtain probabilities for re-ranking. (Section 4)

dynamic_updates.label: Dynamic Intent Space
dynamic_updates.summary: The intent space can be updated without retraining the model by simply adding new (query, intent) pairs to the dense vector index. (Section 4)

experimental_evaluation.label: Experimental Evaluation
experimental_evaluation.summary: The empirical validation of REIC against various baselines using specialized datasets.

dataset_details.label: Dataset Details
dataset_details.summary: The dataset used for testing and training REIC.

training_set_stats.label: Training Set Statistics
training_set_stats.summary: Contains 52,499 training samples: 35,041 from 1P Business and 17,458 from 3P Business. (Section 5.1)

test_set_stats.label: Test Set Statistics
test_set_stats.summary: Consists of 3,647 1P Business queries and 1,717 3P Business queries via random sampling. (Section 5.1)

baseline_models.label: Baseline Models
baseline_models.summary: Comparison models used to evaluate REIC performance.

roberta_baseline.label: RoBERTa-base
roberta_baseline.summary: Fine-tuned with multiple classification heads to categorize utterances across multiple dimensions. (Section 5.2)

mistral_baseline.label: Mistral-7B-v0.3
mistral_baseline.summary: Fine-tuned with a sequence classification head that projects pooled embeddings into a space matching the number of classes. (Section 5.2)

claude_zero_shot.label: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Zero-shot)
claude_zero_shot.summary: Used in a zero-shot configuration with a comprehensive prompt explicitly defining each potential intent. (Section 5.2)

claude_few_shot.label: Claude (Few-shot)
claude_few_shot.summary: Includes 20 demonstration examples (10 per vertical) to enhance coverage of diverse intents. (Section 5.2)

reic_metrics.label: REIC Metric Superiority
reic_metrics.summary: REIC achieved significantly higher Precision, Recall, and F1 scores for both 3P Business (F1: 0.542) and 1P Business (F1: 0.572) verticals compared to Claude+RAG and other baselines. (Table 1)

reic_root.label: RAG-Enhanced Intent Classification (REIC)
reic_root.summary: A novel method designed to address scalability challenges and heterogeneity of intent taxonomies in large-scale customer service systems through a combination of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs).

reic_architecture.label: REIC Architecture
reic_architecture.summary: The technical structural components of the REIC system, combining a retrieval index with a fine-tuned LLM using a hierarchical strategy.

llm_component.label: LLM Component
llm_component.summary: The generative and classification engine of the REIC framework.

mistral_implementation.label: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
mistral_implementation.summary: The specific LLM used in the REIC approach, which is a fine-tuned version of the Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 model. [Section 5.3]

decoder_architecture_hypothesis.label: Decoder-Only Limitation Hypothesis
decoder_architecture_hypothesis.summary: The authors hypothesize that the limited performance of the Mistral Classification model is due to its decoder-only architecture, which may be less effective at extracting the semantic meaning of input queries compared to other architectures. [Section 6.1]

retrieval_component.label: Retrieval Component
retrieval_component.summary: The system responsible for dynamically integrating contextually relevant examples into the classification process.

faiss_index.label: FAISS Retrieval Index
faiss_index.summary: The retrieval index is implemented using FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) to enable efficient similarity search within high-dimensional space. [Section 5.3]

retriever_variants.label: Evaluated Retrievers
retriever_variants.summary: The system experimented with four distinct retrieval algorithms: BM25, MPNet, Contriever-MS MACRO, and ColBERT-v2. [Section 5.3]

classification_strategy.label: Hierarchical Intent Classification
classification_strategy.summary: REIC employs a hierarchical intent classification strategy specifically to reduce overall computational complexity. [Section 7]

evaluation_baselines.label: Evaluation Baselines
evaluation_baselines.summary: The set of comparative models and methods used to benchmark REIC's effectiveness.

claude_rag_baseline.label: Claude + RAG
claude_rag_baseline.summary: A baseline using Claude 3.5 Sonnet as the backbone, where the same set of retrieved candidates used in REIC are incorporated directly into the prompt. [Section 5.2]

claude_rag_purpose.label: Comparative Purpose of Claude+RAG
claude_rag_purpose.summary: Used to assess whether a smaller fine-tuned LLM (like Mistral) can perform competitively against a large foundation model for intent classification. [Section 5.2]

prompting_baselines.label: Prompting-Based Approaches
prompting_baselines.summary: Baseline methods utilizing Claude in Zero-shot and Few-shot configurations. [Section 6.1]

claude_few_shot_performance.label: Claude Few-shot Performance
claude_few_shot_performance.summary: Claude Few-shot achieved a maximum overall F1-score of 0.329. [Section 6.1]

standard_fine_tuning.label: Standard Fine-Tuning
standard_fine_tuning.summary: Traditional LLM fine-tuning approaches, specifically mentioning RoBERTa. [Section 6.1]

roberta_limitation.label: RoBERTa Retraining Requirement
roberta_limitation.summary: While RoBERTa performs reasonably well, it requires extensive retraining whenever new intents emerge in the system. [Section 6.1]

intent_detection_results.label: Intent Detection Ability
intent_detection_results.summary: Comparison of REIC against baselines using Precision, Recall, and F1-score across 3P Business and 1P Business verticals. [Section 6.1]

reic_superiority.label: REIC Overall Performance
reic_superiority.summary: REIC outperforms standard fine-tuning and prompting-based methods, providing greater flexibility and higher precision/recall rates. [Section 6.1]

reic_vs_claude_rag_gap.label: REIC vs Claude+RAG Gap
reic_vs_claude_rag_gap.summary: The Claude + RAG method, while better than standalone prompting, remained inferior to REIC by 26.7%. [Section 6.1]

robustness_unseen_intents.label: Robustness on Unseen Intents
robustness_unseen_intents.summary: Evaluation of the model's ability to generalize to out-of-domain scenarios. [Section 6.2]

ood_scenario_setup.label: Out-of-Domain (OOD) Setup
ood_scenario_setup.summary: Models were trained exclusively on the 3P Business vertical (3 intent categories, ~70 unique intents) and tested on the 1P Business vertical (4 intent categories, >800 unique intent combinations). [Section 6.2]

ood_accuracy_results.label: OOD Accuracy Metrics
ood_accuracy_results.summary: Accuracy results for 1P Business vertical: Claude Zero-shot (0.170), Claude Few-shot (0.308), Claude + RAG (0.389), and REIC (0.283). Overall accuracy for REIC was 0.364. [Section 6.2, Table 2]

system_conclusions.label: System Conclusions
system_conclusions.summary: The final assessment of the REIC method's utility for industry-scale applications.

final_verdict.label: Final Verdict
final_verdict.summary: REIC successfully addresses scalability and taxonomy heterogeneity, outperforming traditional fine-tuning and zero/few-shot approaches on both in-domain and out-of-domain test sets. [Section 7]

concept_retrieval.label: Retrieval Component
concept_retrieval.summary: The mechanism used to retrieve relevant candidates to aid the LLM in intent classification, evaluated across sparse and dense methods.

sub_retriever_types.label: Retriever Types
sub_retriever_types.summary: The specific retrieval algorithms tested within the REIC framework.

fact_mpnet.label: MPNet
fact_mpnet.summary: A sentence embedding model fine-tuned on one billion sentence pairs using a contrastive learning objective. It achieved the highest accuracy in both 3P and 1P Business verticals (Ref: Appendix B/D, Page 6).

fact_contriever.label: Contriever-MS MACRO
fact_contriever.summary: An unsupervised dense retriever pre-trained with contrastive learning and fine-tuned on the MS MARCO dataset. It exhibited the lowest accuracy among tested retrievers (Ref: Appendix B/D, Page 6).

fact_colbertv2.label: ColBERT-v2
fact_colbertv2.summary: A late-interaction retriever that utilizes denoised supervision and residual compression to optimize retrieval quality while reducing the space footprint (Ref: Appendix D, Page 6).

fact_retriever_performance.label: Retriever Performance Comparison
fact_retriever_performance.summary: Overall accuracy results: MPNet (0.564) > ColBERTv2 (0.542) > BM25 (0.532) > Contriever (0.457). MPNet's contrastive learning embeddings are the most effective for REIC (Ref: Appendix B, Page 6).

concept_optimization.label: Retrieval Parameter Optimization
concept_optimization.summary: The process of tuning retrieval settings to balance system performance (accuracy) against operational constraints (latency).

sub_topk_analysis.label: Top-k Candidate Size
sub_topk_analysis.summary: The analysis of how the number of retrieved candidates (top-k) affects the model's output and system speed.

fact_topk_tradeoff.label: Accuracy-Latency Trade-off
fact_topk_tradeoff.summary: Increasing top-k improves accuracy by providing a broader range of relevant information, but results in a sharp rise in inference latency (Ref: Appendix C, Page 6).

fact_topk_selection.label: Optimal Top-k Selection
fact_topk_selection.summary: A value of top-k = 10 was selected to provide a meaningful accuracy boost without excessive computational cost. Requirements vary: real-time systems (chatbots) favor lower top-k, while offline batch processing favors higher top-k (Ref: Appendix C, Page 6).

concept_implementation.label: Implementation Details
concept_implementation.summary: The hardware and software configuration used to train and fine-tune the REIC LLM.

sub_training_config.label: Training Configuration
sub_training_config.summary: The specific technical parameters used for the fine-tuning process.

fact_hardware.label: Compute Infrastructure
fact_hardware.summary: Training utilized 8 NVIDIA-A100 40GB GPUs and 96 vCPUs (Ref: Appendix D, Page 6).

fact_peft_lora.label: PEFT and LoRA Settings
fact_peft_lora.summary: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) was implemented using LoRA adapters with a rank of 8, alpha value of 16, and a dropout rate of 0.1 (Ref: Appendix D, Page 6).

fact_hyperparameters.label: Training Hyperparameters
fact_hyperparameters.summary: Training was conducted for 3 epochs (approximately 3 hours) using Cross Entropy Loss, a training batch size of 8 per GPU, and a learning rate of 2e-5 (Ref: Appendix D, Page 6).

concept_data_privacy.label: Data Anonymization
concept_data_privacy.summary: The protocols implemented to protect sensitive business and customer information.

fact_anonymization_process.label: Anonymization Methodology
fact_anonymization_process.summary: Manual anonymization of labels and transcripts was performed to remove personal information. Product and service names were denonymized to prevent company identification (Ref: Appendix A, Page 6).

standard_rag.label: Standard RAG
standard_rag.summary: A basic RAG system that ranks document chunks based on query similarity.

std_rag_failure_multihop.label: Multi-hop Reasoning Failure
std_rag_failure_multihop.summary: Standard RAG fails on complex questions because queries lack necessary intermediate entities to connect information across different chunks.

std_rag_compression_loss.label: Embedding Compression Loss
std_rag_compression_loss.summary: Important details can be lost during the compression of long chunk embeddings into vectors.

multi_round_rag.label: Multi-Round RAG
multi_round_rag.summary: An approach that decomposes complex questions into sequential sub-queries using the LLM's reasoning abilities.

mr_rag_token_cost.label: High Token Consumption
mr_rag_token_cost.summary: Requires numerous LLM calls (3-6 per round) and up to 8 rounds in total, leading to excessive token costs.

mr_rag_latency.label: Inference Latency
mr_rag_latency.summary: Iterative loops and verbose natural language reasoning chains increase total inference time.

graph_rag.label: Graph RAG
graph_rag.summary: A system that structures the corpus into a knowledge graph to retrieve logically connected information.

gr_rag_construction_cost.label: Graph Construction Expense
gr_rag_construction_cost.summary: The process of offline knowledge graph construction is computationally expensive and time-consuming.

gr_rag_entity_ambiguity.label: Entity Ambiguity
gr_rag_entity_ambiguity.summary: Graph construction is error-prone due to issues with entity ambiguity.

gr_rag_retrieval_redundancy.label: Retrieval Redundancy
gr_rag_retrieval_redundancy.summary: Retrieval from high-degree nodes in the graph leads to redundant and noisy information.

gr_rag_llm_comprehension.label: Graph Structure Difficulty
gr_rag_llm_comprehension.summary: LLMs often struggle to effectively understand and reason over raw graph structures.

t2rag_architecture.label: T2RAG Architecture
t2rag_architecture.summary: The Triplet-driven Thinking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework designed for efficiency and accuracy.

t2rag_triplet_unit.label: Triplet-Centric Unit
t2rag_triplet_unit.summary: T2RAG uses atomic knowledge triplets as the fundamental unit for indexing, retrieval, and reasoning, moving beyond chunks and explicit graphs.

t2rag_graph_free.label: Graph-Free Knowledge Base
t2rag_graph_free.summary: Operates on a database of atomic propositions without building an explicit graph, avoiding indexing costs and link errors.

t2rag_avoid_compression.label: Mitigation of Compression Loss
t2rag_avoid_compression.summary: By using triplets instead of chunks, the system avoids the compression loss inherent in vector embeddings of large text blocks.

t2rag_mechanism.label: Operational Mechanism
t2rag_mechanism.summary: The iterative process of decomposing and resolving queries via triplets.

t2rag_searchable_triplets.label: Searchable Triplets
t2rag_searchable_triplets.summary: The LLM decomposes complex questions into triplets containing placeholders ('?') for unknown entities.

t2rag_iterative_resolution.label: Iterative Resolution
t2rag_iterative_resolution.summary: The system iteratively retrieves evidence from the triplet database to resolve placeholders until all triplets are solved.

t2rag_structured_state.label: Structured State Transition
t2rag_structured_state.summary: Passes compact triplets between iterations rather than verbose natural language, reducing token overhead.

t2rag_performance.label: Empirical Performance
t2rag_performance.summary: Quantifiable gains achieved by T2RAG over state-of-the-art methods.

t2rag_accuracy_gain.label: Accuracy Improvement
t2rag_accuracy_gain.summary: Achieves an average performance gain of up to 11% across six datasets compared to Multi-round and Graph RAG.

t2rag_efficiency_gain.label: Efficiency Improvement
t2rag_efficiency_gain.summary: Reduces inference time and token consumption by up to 45% compared to multi-round methods.

odqa_foundations.label: ODQA Foundations
odqa_foundations.summary: The theoretical basis of Open-Domain Question Answering and Factoid QA.

factoid_qa_definition.label: Factoid QA
factoid_qa_definition.summary: A task where the goal is to extract a small text snippet or a specific entity (person, organization, location) or a yes/no answer from a large corpus.

factoid_qa_challenge.label: Multi-hop Challenge
factoid_qa_challenge.summary: Complex datasets like MusiQue show poor performance (below 50%) due to the need for multi-hop reasoning.

retrieval_granularity.label: Retrieval Granularity
retrieval_granularity.summary: The size of the unit retrieved from the corpus.

chunk_granularity.label: Chunk-level Retrieval
chunk_granularity.summary: Splitting documents into passages of equal token length; often contains a mix of relevant and irrelevant details.

atomic_granularity.label: Atomic-level Retrieval
atomic_granularity.summary: Refining the retrieval unit to the finest elements, such as Entities, to reduce noise and increase precision for complex queries.

knowledge_representation.label: Knowledge Representation Units
knowledge_representation.summary: The hierarchy of granularity used to represent information, ranging from isolated entities to structured triplets and natural language propositions.

entities.label: Entities
entities.summary: The most basic units of information, representing distinct real-world objects.

entity_examples.label: Entity Types
entity_examples.summary: Examples include persons, organizations, or locations.

triplets.label: Triplets (t)
triplets.summary: Structured facts represented as a (subject, predicate, object) tuple.

triplet_structure.label: Canonical Triplet Format
triplet_structure.summary: Formalized as (sub_j ect, predicate, obj ect), representing a single factual statement. (Page 4)

propositions.label: Propositions (p)
propositions.summary: Atomic statements or facts created by converting triplets into natural language sentences.

proposition_utility.label: Semantic Utility of Propositions
proposition_utility.summary: Propositions encapsulate a complete fact in a single sentence, providing greater semantic utility for modern embedding models compared to isolated entities or triplets. (Page 3)

proposition_generation.label: Proposition Verbalization
proposition_generation.summary: Created by concatenating the components of a triplet (e.g., 'subject predicate object'). (Page 4)

related_work.label: Related RAG Paradigms
related_work.summary: An analysis of existing Retrieval-Augmented Generation efforts, categorized into multi-round and graph-enhanced approaches.

query_side_multi_round.label: Query-Side Optimization
query_side_multi_round.summary: Methods focusing on the initial query decomposition or expansion.

khot_decomposition.label: Multi-hop Decomposition
khot_decomposition.summary: Khot et al. (2023) decompose multi-hop questions into single-hop sub-queries solved sequentially. (Page 3)

react_framework.label: ReAct
react_framework.summary: Yao et al. (2023) interleave chain-of-thought (CoT) steps with search actions issued by the LLM. (Page 3)

query2doc.label: Query2Doc
query2doc.summary: Wang et al. (2023b) expand queries into concise triplets to reduce token usage while preserving recall. (Page 3)

intermediate_result_multi_round.label: Intermediate Result Iteration
intermediate_result_multi_round.summary: Methods that rely on generated results to guide the next retrieval iteration.

beam_retrieval.label: Beam Retrieval
beam_retrieval.summary: Zhang et al. (2024a) jointly train an encoder and classifiers to maintain multiple passage hypotheses across hops. (Page 3)

flare_generation.label: FLARE
flare_generation.summary: Jiang et al. (2023) forecast upcoming sentences to trigger fresh retrieval during long-form generation. (Page 3)

ircot_iterretgen.label: IRCoT and ITER-RETGEN
ircot_iterretgen.summary: Trivedi et al. (2023) and Shao et al. (2023) alternately expand CoT and fetch evidence for multi-step questions. (Page 3)

adaptive_qa.label: Adaptive QA
adaptive_qa.summary: Xie et al. (2023) employ a framework that selects the simplest effective retrieval strategy based on query complexity. (Page 3)

odqa_vs_kgqa.label: ODQA vs KGQA
odqa_vs_kgqa.summary: Open Domain QA (ODQA) differs from KGQA in two ways: it is grounded in unstructured text and prioritizes final answering accuracy over retrieval precision. (Page 3)

graphrag_community.label: GraphRAG (Edge et al.)
graphrag_community.summary: Constructs a knowledge graph using LLMs and utilizes community detection for hierarchical summarization and retrieval. (Page 3)

lightrag_dual.label: LightRAG
lightrag_dual.summary: Guo et al. (2024) introduce a dual-level retrieval system combining graph structures with vector search. (Page 3)

minirag_heterogeneous.label: MiniRAG
minirag_heterogeneous.summary: Fan et al. (2025) build a heterogeneous graph of text chunks and named entities for Small Language Models (SLMs). (Page 3)

hipporag_synonym.label: HippoRAG / HippoRAG2
hipporag_synonym.summary: Gutiérrez et al. (2025) create synonym links between similar entities and use PageRank for final node selection. (Page 3)

graph_rag_drawbacks.label: Graph RAG Limitations
graph_rag_drawbacks.summary: Graph construction from unstructured text is costly and error-prone; neighbor expansion (retrieving all triplets sharing a head/tail entity) is often inaccurate and computationally expensive. (Page 3)

t2rag_framework.label: T2RAG Framework
t2rag_framework.summary: A two-stage process (Offline Indexing and Online Retrieval) that skips explicit graph construction while retaining multi-hop reasoning.

offline_indexing.label: Offline Indexing
offline_indexing.summary: The process of transforming a raw text corpus C into a graph-free knowledge base of atomic propositions.

indexing_motivation.label: Motivation for Proposition Granularity
indexing_motivation.summary: Propositions are used because they encode unambiguous facts (unlike entity level) and avoid compression loss (unlike chunk level). (Page 4)

canonical_triplet_generation.label: Canonical Triplet Generation
canonical_triplet_generation.summary: Using an information extraction model (LLM_IE) to perform Open Information Extraction (OpenIE) to extract sets of triplets T_i from document chunks c_i. (Page 4)

openie_definition.label: OpenIE
openie_definition.summary: Open Information Extraction identifies key facts as triplets without a pre-defined schema. (Page 4)

triplet_embedding_step.label: Triplet Embedding
triplet_embedding_step.summary: The process of converting triplets into natural language propositions to maximize semantic utility for embedding models. (Page 4)

triplet_vector_db.label: Triplet Vector DB Construction
triplet_vector_db.summary: The process of encoding propositions P_total into dense vectors and indexing them for similarity search. (Page 4)

faiss_indexing.label: FAISS Indexing
faiss_indexing.summary: High-performance vector search library (FAISS) is used to create index I for rapid similarity search across propositions. (Page 4)

source_mapping.label: Source Chunk Mapping
source_mapping.summary: T2RAG saves the mapping from propositions to their original source chunks, as original text is necessary for accuracy. (Page 4)

online_retrieval.label: Online Retrieval
online_retrieval.summary: An iterative, adaptive process of resolving query triplets by eliminating '?' placeholders via RAG.

adaptive_retrieval_strategy.label: Adaptive Retrieval Strategy
adaptive_retrieval_strategy.summary: Instead of a fixed top-k, T2RAG adopts a strategy based on query complexity and utilizes a multi-round paradigm to handle multi-hop questions. (Page 4)

triplet_based_adaptive_retrieval.label: Step 2.1: Triplet-Based Adaptive Retrieval
triplet_based_adaptive_retrieval.summary: The process of converting searchable triplets into query propositions for embedding and indexing. (Page 4)

retrieval_constraint.label: Retrieval Constraints
retrieval_constraint.summary: The system retrieves based on triplets but constrains the total number of triplets by the number of associated chunks to ensure relevance and diversity. (Page 4)

triplet_types.label: Triplet Categorization
triplet_types.summary: Classification of triplets based on the number of placeholders ('?') they contain to determine their searchability.

t_resolved.label: Resolved Triplets (Tresolved)
t_resolved.summary: Triplets with zero placeholders, representing fully known facts that require no further search.

t_searchable.label: Searchable Triplets (Tsearchable)
t_searchable.summary: Triplets with exactly one placeholder; the presence of two known elements enables focused and accurate retrieval.

t_fuzzy.label: Fuzzy Triplets (Tfuzzy)
t_fuzzy.summary: Triplets with two or more placeholders; these are too ambiguous for direct search and must be resolved in subsequent iterations.

step_2_1.label: Step 2.1: Triplet-Based Adaptive Retrieval
step_2_1.summary: The retrieval of supporting context based on searchable triplets using adaptive strategies.

adaptive_strat_1.label: Unique Source Chunk Constraint
adaptive_strat_1.summary: Retrieval continues until context from k unique source chunks of triplets has been retrieved.

adaptive_strat_2.label: Global Candidate Ranking
adaptive_strat_2.summary: Retrieval candidates from all query propositions are aggregated into a unified pool and ranked globally by similarity scores rather than using separate budgets per proposition.

retrieval_output.label: Retrieval Output Set
retrieval_output.summary: The process returns a set of retrieved propositions P(l)retrieved and their corresponding source chunks C(l)retrieved to fill missing details in triplets.

step_2_2.label: Step 2.2: Resolving Triplets with Retrieved Context
step_2_2.summary: Using an LLM to populate placeholders within triplets using the retrieved propositions and chunks.

resolution_upgrade.label: Triplet Upgrade Path
resolution_upgrade.summary: The LLM transforms triplets by filling placeholders: Searchable triplets become Resolved; Fuzzy triplets may become Searchable or Resolved.

step_2_3.label: Step 2.3: State Update
step_2_3.summary: The system updates internal state to maintain focus and efficiency for the next iteration.

state_monotonic.label: Monotonic Augmentation
state_monotonic.summary: The collection of resolved triplets is monotonically augmented with any facts verified in the current round.

state_focus.label: Targeted Search
state_focus.summary: The system targets only newly searchable triplets for the next iteration, avoiding re-scanning previous ones.

state_pruning.label: Fuzzy Queue Pruning
state_pruning.summary: Fuzzy triplets are removed from the queue if they are successfully resolved or promoted to a searchable state.

state_fallback.label: Dense Retrieval Fallback
state_fallback.summary: If no searchable triplets are identified, the system uses the embedding of the natural language query to perform dense retrieval against the triplet vector database.

state_efficiency.label: Token Overhead Reduction
state_efficiency.summary: By passing compact triplets instead of verbose Chain-of-Thought reasoning, T2RAG reduces token overhead and ensures semantic alignment with the retrieval index.

step_2_4.label: Step 2.4: Termination and Final Answer Synthesis
step_2_4.summary: The logic for ending the iterative loop and generating the final grounded answer.

term_conditions.label: Termination Conditions
term_conditions.summary: Loop ends if: (1) Searchable and fuzzy queues are empty; (2) No new searchables generated and no fuzzies remain; or (3) Maximum iterations (N) are reached.

synth_path_a.label: Successful Completion Pathway
synth_path_a.summary: If all triplets are resolved, the LLM generates the answer based on the original query and the set of fully resolved triplets.

synth_path_b.label: Forced Termination Pathway
synth_path_b.summary: If loop stops due to limits or failure to generate searchables, context is constructed from all accumulated resolved and remaining searchable triplets.

exp_setup.label: Experimental Setup
exp_setup.summary: Evaluation parameters used to validate the T2RAG framework.

impl_details.label: Implementation Technicalities
impl_details.summary: Embeddings: NV-Embed-v2. LLMs: Gemini-2.5-flash or GPT-4o-mini. Chunking: 1200 tokens with 100-token overlap. Retrieval: k=5. Iterations: N=3. Metrics: Exact Match (EM) and F1.

triplet_driven_thinking.label: Triplet-Driven Thinking
triplet_driven_thinking.summary: The process of decomposing complex queries into atomic triplets to guide retrieval.

triplet_decomposition_fact.label: Query Decomposition
triplet_decomposition_fact.summary: T2RAG decomposes complex queries into atomic triplets which are then resolved against a triplet knowledge base.

triplet_resolution_impact.label: Impact of Triplet Resolution
triplet_resolution_impact.summary: The correlation between successful triplet resolution and final answer accuracy.

resolution_performance_gap.label: Resolution Performance Gap
resolution_performance_gap.summary: Significant delta in performance based on whether triplets are fully resolved.

resolution_performance_gap_data.label: 2Wiki Resolution Data
resolution_performance_gap_data.summary: On the 2Wiki dataset, F1 score drops from 76% (resolved) to 53% (unresolved). (Page 7)

error_source_analysis.label: Error Source Analysis
error_source_analysis.summary: Analysis of incorrect answers using LLMs.

retrieval_failure_fact.label: Primary Error Cause
retrieval_failure_fact.summary: Missing retrieval is the leading cause of incorrect answers. (Page 7)

hallucination_rate_fact.label: Hallucination Rate
hallucination_rate_fact.summary: Hallucinations account for as low as 2% of errors. (Page 7)

iterative_reasoning_module.label: Iterative Reasoning Module
iterative_reasoning_module.summary: A multi-round retrieval and resolution process essential for complex problem solving.

multi_hop_essential_fact.label: Multi-hop Necessity
multi_hop_essential_fact.summary: Multi-round retrieval is critical for decomposing multi-hop QA; removing it causes a 54.5% drop in F1 score on the MuSiQue dataset. (Page 7)

hybrid_context_utilization.label: Hybrid Context Utilization
hybrid_context_utilization.summary: The combination of triplet retrieval and raw text chunks.

raw_chunk_complement_fact.label: Raw Chunk Role
raw_chunk_complement_fact.summary: Raw chunk text complements the missing details that triplets alone may not provide. (Page 7)

sota_performance.label: State-of-the-Art Performance
sota_performance.summary: T2RAG leads in average EM and F1 scores across LLM backbones.

em_precision_fact.label: EM Precision
em_precision_fact.summary: Pronounced advantage in Exact Match (EM) is attributed to the precision of triplet-based retrieval in identifying exact entities for factoid QA. (Page 7)

multi_hop_superiority.label: Multi-hop QA Superiority
multi_hop_superiority.summary: T2RAG significantly outperforms single-round and multi-round baselines on complex datasets like 2Wiki.

ircot_comparison_fact.label: IRCoT Comparison
ircot_comparison_fact.summary: Outperforms IRCoT in EM by over 7.7% (Gemini-2.5-flash) and 5.4% (GPT-4o-mini) on 2Wiki. (Page 7)

llm_synergy.label: LLM Synergy
llm_synergy.summary: Effectiveness of T2RAG when paired with different types of LLMs.

reasoning_llm_boost.label: Reasoning LLM Boost
reasoning_llm_boost.summary: T2RAG leverages advanced reasoning capabilities of models like Gemini-2.5-flash more effectively than GPT-4o-mini due to its step-by-step guidance. (Page 7)

filtering_bottleneck_hypothesis.label: Filtering Bottleneck Hypothesis
filtering_bottleneck_hypothesis.summary: Methods like HippoRAG2 decrease in performance with reasoning LLMs because they relegate the LLM to simple filtering, failing to harness reasoning capabilities. (Page 7)

iterative_process_contribution.label: Iterative Process Contribution
iterative_process_contribution.summary: Removing the iterative reasoning module causes significant degradation, especially on multi-hop QA. (Page 7)

chunk_text_contribution.label: Chunk Text Contribution
chunk_text_contribution.summary: Removing raw chunk text during iteration substantially harms performance. (Page 7)

efficiency_analysis.label: Computational Efficiency (RQ4)
efficiency_analysis.summary: Analysis of token consumption and latency during indexing and retrieval.

indexing_cost.label: Indexing Cost
indexing_cost.summary: The one-time offline cost of processing the corpus into triplets.

graph_rag_comparison_fact.label: Graph RAG Token Comparison
graph_rag_comparison_fact.summary: While T2RAG indexing is high, it is lower than LightRAG (6x) and GraphRAG (10x) total token consumption. (Page 8)

online_retrieval_efficiency.label: Online Retrieval Efficiency
online_retrieval_efficiency.summary: The cost and speed of the retrieval phase during query time.

retrieval_efficiency_fact.label: Retrieval Efficiency
retrieval_efficiency_fact.summary: More efficient in tokens and latency than IRCoT and comparable to single-round methods because it targets triplets rather than noisy text chunks. (Page 8)

scaling_behavior.label: Context Scaling (RQ5)
scaling_behavior.summary: Analysis of performance relative to the number of retrieved documents (top-k).

top_k_robustness_fact.label: Top-k Robustness
top_k_robustness_fact.summary: T2RAG reaches the performance plateau (0.7) faster than baselines and is less dependent on scaling up the volume of retrieved text. (Page 8)

llm_backbones.label: LLM Backbones
llm_backbones.summary: The models used to drive the RAG process.

paradigm_shift.label: Reasoning-Driven Synthesis Paradigm
paradigm_shift.summary: The fundamental approach of T2RAG which prioritizes deliberate reasoning and the use of atomic facts over unstructured data retrieval.

atomic_fact_synthesis.label: Synthesis of Atomic Facts
atomic_fact_synthesis.summary: The process of replacing unstructured context retrieval and generation with a more deliberate synthesis of discrete, atomic pieces of information.

experimental_limits.label: Experimental Constraints
experimental_limits.summary: Limitations imposed during the testing phase regarding iterations and model selection.

iteration_limit.label: Iteration Constraint
iteration_limit.summary: Multi-round methods were limited to 3 iterations to match dataset complexity and ensure fair efficiency comparisons. (Section 7)

embedding_model_limit.label: Model Testing Constraints
embedding_model_limit.summary: Insufficient resources to test LLM-based embedding models or re-rankers. (Section 7)

kg_resource_limit.label: Knowledge Graph Constraints
kg_resource_limit.summary: Lack of testing on large external knowledge graphs, specifically mentioning the Wikipedia KG (Hertling and Paulheim, 2018). (Section 7)

evaluation_limits.label: Evaluation Constraints
evaluation_limits.summary: Constraints related to how the system's performance was measured.

black_box_eval.label: Black-Box Evaluation
black_box_eval.summary: Evaluation is limited to black-box and end-to-end metrics, resulting in a lack of explainability due to the absence of recall scores for specific chunks. (Section 7)

methodological_limits.label: Methodological Constraints
methodological_limits.summary: Technical weaknesses in the information extraction and representation pipeline.

triplet_dependency.label: Triplet Extraction Dependency
triplet_dependency.summary: The approach is highly dependent on the quality of the initial triplet extraction. (Section 7)

relationship_complexity.label: Complex Knowledge Representation
relationship_complexity.summary: Simple triplets may fail to adequately represent complex knowledge such as many-to-many relationships. (Section 7)

extraction_efficiency.label: OpenIE Pipeline Efficiency
extraction_efficiency.summary: The efficiency of triplet extraction can be improved beyond the classic OpenIE pipeline, requiring further efforts in the Information Extraction (Grishman, 2015) area. (Section 7)

scalability_limits.label: Scalability Constraints
scalability_limits.summary: Challenges associated with processing extremely large datasets.

token_intensity.label: Indexing Token Cost
token_intensity.summary: Building the index from a very large corpus is token-intensive. (Section 7)

system_advantages.label: System Advantages
system_advantages.summary: Strengths of T2RAG compared to existing Graph RAG approaches.

pre_existing_kg_efficiency.label: Pre-existing Database Efficiency
pre_existing_kg_efficiency.summary: T2RAG is highly efficient when utilizing a pre-existing triplet database. (Section 7)

evolving_kb_support.label: Incremental Knowledge Updates
evolving_kb_support.summary: T2RAG is inherently suitable for evolving knowledge bases because new triplets are independent of previous ones and can be added incrementally, unlike static Graph RAG approaches (Zhang et al., 2025). (Section 7)

hypergraph_modeling.label: Hyper-graph Modeling
hypergraph_modeling.summary: Using hyper-graph modeling (Luo et al., 2025) to address the challenge of representing many-to-many relationships in knowledge extraction. (Section 7)

robustness_and_security.label: Robustness and Security
robustness_and_security.summary: Future study into the adversarial robustness (Qi et al., 2026) and unlearning problems (Geng et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2025a,b) of the RAG system. (Section 7)

optimization_studies.label: System Compression
optimization_studies.summary: Future research into compression techniques (Hashemi et al., 2024; Gong et al., 2025) given the evolving nature of knowledge bases. (Section 7)

core_rag.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
core_rag.summary: The foundational framework of retrieving external documents to augment LLM prompts for improved accuracy and reduced hallucination in knowledge-intensive NLP.

fact_lewis_2020.label: Foundational RAG Framework
fact_lewis_2020.summary: Introduced retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks to combine parametric and non-parametric memory (Petroni et al., 2020).

fact_shao_2023.label: Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy
fact_shao_2023.summary: Enhancement of RAG via a synergy where retrieval and generation occur iteratively to refine the final output (Shao et al., 2023).

fact_sarthi_2024.label: RAPTOR (Recursive Abstractive Processing)
fact_sarthi_2024.summary: A method for tree-organized retrieval using recursive abstractive processing to handle multi-scale information (Sarthi et al., 2024).

fact_sawarkar_2024.label: Blended RAG
fact_sawarkar_2024.summary: Improving accuracy by combining semantic search with hybrid query-based retrievers (Sawarkar et al., 2024).

fact_tang_2024.label: MultiHop-RAG Benchmarking
fact_tang_2024.summary: A benchmark specifically designed to evaluate RAG performance on multi-hop queries (Tang & Yang, 2024).

fact_nie_2019.label: Semantic Retrieval Importance
fact_nie_2019.summary: Analysis revealing the criticality of semantic retrieval for machine reading at scale (Nie et al., 2019).

fact_yang_2019.label: BERTSerini Open-Domain QA
fact_yang_2019.summary: End-to-end open-domain question answering utilizing BERT and Serini for efficient retrieval (Yang et al., 2019).

fact_li_2025.label: Roles of Graphs in RAG
fact_li_2025.summary: Investigation into the specific roles that graphs and LLMs play in KG-based retrieval-augmented generation (Li et al., 2025).

fact_luo_2025_hyper.label: HypergraphRAG
fact_luo_2025_hyper.summary: A RAG approach using hypergraph-structured knowledge representation to capture complex N-ary relations (Luo et al., 2025).

fact_peng_2024.label: GraphRAG Survey
fact_peng_2024.summary: A comprehensive survey of current methodologies in Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Peng et al., 2024).

fact_shen_2024.label: GEAR (Graph-Enhanced Agent)
fact_shen_2024.summary: A graph-enhanced agent designed to optimize the RAG process via structured knowledge (Shen et al., 2024).

fact_sun_2024.label: Think-on-Graph
fact_sun_2024.summary: A framework for deep and responsible LLM reasoning specifically over Knowledge Graphs (Sun et al., 2024).

fact_xiang_2025.label: Graph Utility Analysis
fact_xiang_2025.summary: A comprehensive analysis determining the specific scenarios where graphs provide an advantage in RAG (Xiang et al., 2025).

fact_zhou_2025.label: Unified Graph-RAG Framework
fact_zhou_2025.summary: An in-depth analysis of graph-based RAG within a unified experimental framework (Zhou et al., 2025).

fact_mavromatis_2024.label: GNN-RAG
fact_mavromatis_2024.summary: The use of Graph Neural Networks for retrieval to support LLM reasoning (Mavromatis & Karypis, 2024).

kg_integration.label: Knowledge Graph (KG) Integration
kg_integration.summary: Technical methods for building, adapting, and interfacing Knowledge Graphs with LLMs for Question Answering (KGQA).

fact_ma_2025.label: LLM-KG Synthesis for QA
fact_ma_2025.summary: A synthesis of opportunities and methods where LLMs meet KGs for question answering (Ma et al., 2025).

fact_martinez_2018.label: OpenIE KG Construction
fact_martinez_2018.summary: An approach using Open Information Extraction (OpenIE) to construct knowledge graphs from raw text (Martinez-Rodriguez et al., 2018).

fact_tian_2024.label: KG-Adapter
fact_tian_2024.summary: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) method to enable KG integration into LLMs (Tian et al., 2024).

fact_wu_2023.label: Retrieve-Rewrite-Answer
fact_wu_2023.summary: A framework for KGQA that enhances LLMs by converting KG data to text (KG-to-Text) (Wu et al., 2023).

fact_xu_2025.label: Adaptive Multi-Aspect Retrieval
fact_xu_2025.summary: Harnessing LLMs for KGQA via adaptive retrieval that considers multiple aspects of a query (Xu et al., 2025).

fact_oguz_2020.label: UniK-QA
fact_oguz_2020.summary: Unified representations of both structured (KG) and unstructured (text) knowledge for open-domain QA (Oguz et al., 2020).

fact_wei_2022.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
fact_wei_2022.summary: Prompting technique that elicits a series of intermediate reasoning steps to improve LLM performance on complex tasks (Wei et al., 2022).

fact_luo_2024.label: Faithful Graph Reasoning
fact_luo_2024.summary: Focuses on making LLM reasoning over graphs more faithful and interpretable (Luo et al., 2024).

fact_su_2024.label: Semi-structured CoT
fact_su_2024.summary: Integrating multiple knowledge sources into a semi-structured chain-of-thought to improve reasoning (Su et al., 2024).

fact_trivedi_2023.label: Interleaved Retrieval-CoT
fact_trivedi_2023.summary: Interleaving the retrieval process with Chain-of-Thought reasoning for knowledge-intensive multi-step questions (Trivedi et al., 2023).

fact_zliu_2025d.label: Symbolic Reasoning over Time Series
fact_zliu_2025d.summary: Evaluating if LLMs can adequately perform symbolic reasoning on time-series data (Z. Liu et al., 2025d).

fact_yliu_2025c.label: Hypervector Reasoning
fact_yliu_2025c.summary: Exploring if hypervectors are sufficient for single-call LLM reasoning over knowledge graphs (Y. Liu et al., 2025c).

fact_mavromatis_2022.label: ReaRev
fact_mavromatis_2022.summary: An adaptive reasoning framework for question answering over knowledge graphs (Mavromatis & Karypis, 2022).

knowledge_dynamics.label: Knowledge Dynamics & Management
knowledge_dynamics.summary: Studies on how LLMs store knowledge, the conflicts between internal (parametric) and external (non-parametric) knowledge, and how to remove knowledge (unlearning).

fact_mallen_2023.label: Parametric vs. Non-Parametric Memory
fact_mallen_2023.summary: Investigation into when to trust internal LLM weights (parametric) versus retrieved documents (non-parametric) (Mallen et al., 2023).

fact_yliu_2025a.label: Lune (Efficient Unlearning)
fact_yliu_2025a.summary: LLM unlearning via LoRA fine-tuning using negative examples (Y. Liu et al., 2025a).

fact_yliu_2025b.label: Recover-to-Forget
fact_yliu_2025b.summary: Efficient unlearning through gradient reconstruction from LoRA (Y. Liu et al., 2025b).

fact_xie_2023.label: Knowledge Conflict Behavior
fact_xie_2023.summary: Analysis of LLM behavior ('adaptive chameleon' vs 'stubborn sloth') when parametric and retrieved knowledge conflict (Xie et al., 2023).

fact_press_2023.label: Compositionality Gap
fact_press_2023.summary: Measuring the gap in LLMs' ability to compose multiple known facts to reach a conclusion (Press et al., 2023).

evaluation_benchmarks.summary: Standardized datasets and benchmarks used to measure retrieval, embedding, and reasoning performance.

fact_muennighoff_2023.label: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark)
fact_muennighoff_2023.summary: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating text embedding models across diverse tasks (Muennighoff et al., 2023).

fact_yang_2018.summary: A dataset designed for multi-hop question answering requiring reasoning over multiple documents (Yang et al., 2018).
