fact_trivedi_2022.summary: A benchmark for multi-hop questions created via single-hop question composition (Trivedi et al., 2022).

fact_voorhees_2000.label: TREC-8 QA Track
fact_voorhees_2000.summary: Early foundational work in question answering benchmarks from the TREC-8 conference (Voorhees & Tice, 2000).

fact_qi_2026.label: RAG Attack & Defense Benchmarking
fact_qi_2026.summary: Benchmarking attacks on knowledge extraction and corresponding defenses within RAG systems (Qi et al., 2026).

t2rag_methodology.label: T2RAG Methodology
t2rag_methodology.summary: The operational workflow of T2RAG, consisting of query decomposition, iterative triplet resolution, and final answer generation.

main_process.label: Main Process (Algorithm 1)
main_process.summary: The primary control flow for Online Iterative Triplet Resolution.

step_1_decomp.label: Structured Query Decomposition
step_1_decomp.summary: The initial stage where the LLM decomposes the query q into resolved triplets (Tresolved), searchable triplets (Tsearchable), and fuzzy triplets (Tfuzzy).

step_2_resolving.label: Multi-Round Triplet Resolving Loop
step_2_resolving.summary: An iterative loop (up to K iterations) that resolves searchable and fuzzy triplets using adaptive retrieval and LLM resolution.

step_2_1_adaptive.label: Adaptive Retrieval Call
step_2_1_adaptive.summary: Calls the ADAPTIVERETRIEVE function using Tsearchable, index I, target chunks k, and map Mchunk to obtain retrieved propositions (Pretrieved) and chunks (Cretrieved).

step_2_2_llm_resolve.label: LLM-based Triplets Resolution
step_2_2_llm_resolve.summary: The LLM resolves current searchable and fuzzy triplets based on the retrieved information to update the set of resolved and searchable triplets.

step_2_3_state_update.label: State Update
step_2_3_state_update.summary: Updates Tresolved and Tsearchable and removes newly resolved or searchable triplets from the fuzzy set Tfuzzy.

step_3_answering.label: Final Answering
step_3_answering.summary: The LLM generates the final answer 'a' using the original query 'q' and the accumulated context Tcontext (Tresolved union Tsearchable).

adaptive_retrieval.label: Adaptive Triplet Retrieval (Algorithm 2)
adaptive_retrieval.summary: A function that converts searchable triplets into propositions to retrieve relevant document chunks.

prop_generation.label: Proposition Generation
prop_generation.summary: Concatenates each triplet t in Tsearchable into a query proposition and generates a query vector using an embedding model E.

similarity_search.label: Similarity Search
similarity_search.summary: Searches the index I using query vectors to find candidate propositions (Pcandidates) and sorts them globally by similarity score.

chunk_selection.label: Unique Chunk Selection
chunk_selection.summary: Iterates through sorted Pcandidates to collect unique chunks from Mchunk until the target number of chunks 'k' is reached.

comparative_baselines.label: Comparative Baselines
comparative_baselines.summary: Other RAG and reasoning methods used to evaluate T2RAG's performance.

ircot.label: IRCoT
ircot.summary: An iterative reasoning method based on Chain-of-Thought (CoT).

ircot_process.label: IRCoT Cycle
ircot_process.summary: Operates on an iterative cycle: generating a reasoning step ('thought') and then acting upon it (Page 14).

ircot_prompt.label: IRCoT CoT Prompt
ircot_prompt.summary: Instructs the model to generate one reasoning step at a time across multiple documents, concluding with 'So the answer is:' when finished (Page 14).

hipporag2.label: HippoRAG2
hipporag2.summary: A graph-based RAG approach utilizing entity-aware retrieval.

hipporag_mechanism.label: HippoRAG2 Mechanism
hipporag_mechanism.summary: Builds a knowledge graph from text and uses Personalized PageRank (PPR) for entity-aware retrieval (Page 14).

hipporag_filtering.label: HippoRAG2 Fact Filtering
hipporag_filtering.summary: Uses a high-stakes QA prompt to filter candidate facts, selecting up to 4 relevant facts in a JSON format: {'fact': [['s1', 'p1', 'o1'], ...]} (Page 14).

hipporag_hyperparams.label: HippoRAG2 Hyperparameters
hipporag_hyperparams.summary: Specific settings: Synonym Threshold = 0.8 (cosine similarity for merging entities), Damping Factor (PPR) = 0.5, Temperature = 0.0 (Table 2, Page 15).

raptor_mod.label: RAPTOR Modification
raptor_mod.summary: The Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) for clustering was replaced with K-Means for superior computational efficiency while maintaining similar quality (Page 14).

raptor_params.label: RAPTOR Parameters
raptor_params.summary: Cluster size is set to 10 and level is set to 3 (Page 14).

llm_temp.label: LLM Temperature
llm_temp.summary: Set to 0 to ensure deterministic and reproducible outputs (Page 14).

hardware.label: Hardware Configuration
hardware.summary: Local embedding generation performed on a single NVIDIA L40S GPU (Page 14).

answer_standardization.label: Answer Format Standardization
answer_standardization.summary: Modified prompts to include a specific format template, which provided a significant performance boost over baseline implementations (Page 14).

dataset_stats.label: Dataset Statistics
dataset_stats.summary: The corpora used for evaluation including PopQA, 2Wiki, Musique, HotpotQA, Story, and Medical (Table 3, Page 15).

analysis_findings.label: Analysis and Findings
analysis_findings.summary: The conclusions drawn from the experimental results regarding T2RAG's effectiveness.

performance_gap.label: Comparative Performance
performance_gap.summary: T2RAG consistently achieved the highest average EM and F1 scores; IRCoT was the second-best; HippoRAG2 was significantly lower, often comparable to standard RAG (Page 15).

reasoning_hypothesis.label: The Reasoning Hypothesis
reasoning_hypothesis.summary: T2RAG's strength lies in leveraging the advanced reasoning of modern LLMs. Architecture that relegates LLMs to simpler tasks (like filtering in HippoRAG2) creates a bottleneck that prevents unlocking full LLM potential (Page 15).

hop_complexity_analysis.label: Hop Complexity Analysis
hop_complexity_analysis.summary: Analysis of how T2RAG performs as the number of reasoning steps (hops) increases, specifically using the MuSiQue dataset.

fact_state_of_art_2_3_hop.label: State-of-the-Art 2 and 3-Hop Performance
fact_state_of_art_2_3_hop.summary: T2RAG consistently achieves State-of-the-Art (SOTA) performance on queries requiring 2 and 3 reasoning hops (Page 16).

fact_hippo_rag_4_hop.label: HippoRAG2 Advantage at 4-Hops
fact_hippo_rag_4_hop.summary: At extreme hop counts (4-hop), graph traversal methods like HippoRAG2 exhibit an advantage due to their global graph connectivity (Page 16).

fact_t2rag_recommendation.label: T2RAG Recommended Reasoning Depth
fact_t2rag_recommendation.summary: T2RAG is specifically recommended for questions requiring reasoning depths of up to 3 hops (Page 16).

indexing_stage_analysis.label: Indexing Stage Analysis
indexing_stage_analysis.summary: Analysis of the one-time offline process of preparing the knowledge base.

fact_indexing_nature.label: Indexing Stage Nature
fact_indexing_nature.summary: The indexing stage is a one-time, offline process that can be substantial and potentially prohibitive for very large corpora (Page 16).

fact_non_linear_scaling.label: Non-Linear Indexing Cost
fact_non_linear_scaling.summary: Indexing costs (time and tokens) for T2RAG triplet extraction and RAPTOR summarization do not scale linearly with document count; cost depends on the informativeness and density of source documents (Page 16).

retrieval_stage_analysis.label: Retrieval Stage Analysis
retrieval_stage_analysis.summary: Analysis of the online process occurring for every query, where efficiency is critical for user-facing applications.

fact_t2rag_vs_hipporag2_retrieval.label: T2RAG vs HippoRAG2 Efficiency
fact_t2rag_vs_hipporag2_retrieval.summary: T2RAG is as efficient as HippoRAG2 during retrieval, exhibiting similar time and token consumption profiles because both operate over graph structures (Page 17).

fact_t2rag_vs_ircot_efficiency.label: T2RAG vs IRCoT Efficiency
fact_t2rag_vs_ircot_efficiency.summary: T2RAG is substantially more efficient than multi-round RAG methods like IRCoT, achieving over 45% reduction in token consumption in Medical and Story datasets by synthesizing answers in a single round rather than iterative refinement (Page 17).

fact_t2rag_vs_raptor_efficiency.label: T2RAG vs RAPTOR Efficiency
fact_t2rag_vs_raptor_efficiency.summary: T2RAG often achieves lower or comparable token consumption than RAPTOR because it generates concise answers directly from structured triplets, minimizing output tokens (Page 17).

efficiency_metrics.label: Efficiency Metrics
efficiency_metrics.summary: The specific formulas and measurements used to quantify computational cost.

fact_token_consumption_formula.label: Token Consumption Formula
fact_token_consumption_formula.summary: Token Consumption = (#input tokens) + 4 * (#output tokens). This weighting reflects LLM API pricing where generation (output) is typically 4x the cost of processing (input) (Page 17).

fact_time_measurement.label: Time Measurement
fact_time_measurement.summary: Wall-clock time is measured in seconds. In visualization, retrieval stage time is scaled by 1000 to remain visible alongside the larger indexing times (Page 17).

architectural_validation.label: Architectural Validation
architectural_validation.summary: Studies conducted to prove the necessity of specific design choices in T2RAG.

ablation_study_triplets.label: Triplet Embedding Ablation Study
ablation_study_triplets.summary: Comparison between T2RAG (triplet-based) and a 'Chunk-based Slot-Filling' baseline.

fact_ablation_f1_drop.label: F1 Score Degradation
fact_ablation_f1_drop.summary: Removing triplet-based retrieval results in a drastic performance decline, with F1 scores dropping by approximately 40-60% across all datasets (Page 18).

fact_granularity_mismatch.label: Granularity Mismatch Theory
fact_granularity_mismatch.summary: Chunk-based retrieval fails because the embedding of a specific decomposed query slot lacks precise semantic alignment ('hook') with the coarser embedding of a large text chunk (Page 18).

fact_premature_termination.label: Premature Loop Termination
fact_premature_termination.summary: The chunk-based baseline shows a significantly lower number of 'Calls,' indicating the iterative loop breaks early because the system fails to retrieve relevant information to fill reasoning slots (Page 18).

iteration_analysis.label: Iteration Analysis
iteration_analysis.summary: Evaluation of the number of retrieval iterations required relative to the number of retrieved chunks (top-k).

fact_t2rag_k_stability.label: T2RAG top-k Stability
fact_t2rag_k_stability.summary: T2RAG's iterations remain stable and low (between 1.54 and 1.73) regardless of the k value, due to focused retrieval guided by triplet placeholders (Page 18).

fact_ircot_k_dependency.label: IRCoT top-k Dependency
fact_ircot_k_dependency.summary: IRCoT shows a complex relationship with k; as k increases from 4 to 6, iterations surprisingly decrease, indicating its dependence on chunk quantity and effectiveness (Page 18).

multi_round_comparison.label: Multi-round Method Comparison
multi_round_comparison.summary: Comparison of T2RAG against agentic baselines ReAct and Self-Ask.

fact_agentic_settings.label: Agentic Comparison Settings
fact_agentic_settings.summary: Comparisons were conducted with k = 5 for document retrieval and a maximum limit of 3 iterations (Page 18).

fact_iteration_reduction_vs_ircot.label: Iteration Reduction vs IRCoT
fact_iteration_reduction_vs_ircot.summary: T2RAG consistently saves on retrieval iterations compared to IRCoT. At k = 2, T2RAG requires 1.54 iterations vs IRCoT's 1.85, a reduction of approximately 17% (Page 18).

comparison_baselines.label: Comparison Baselines
comparison_baselines.summary: Multi-round agents used to benchmark T2RAG performance.

fact_baselines_list.label: Benchmarked Baselines
fact_baselines_list.summary: T2RAG is compared against ReAct and Self-Ask agents using Gemini-2.5 Flash and GPT-4o-mini models. (Page 19)

fact_token_advantage.label: Token Usage Efficiency
fact_token_advantage.summary: T2RAG achieves comparable or superior results to ReAct and Self-Ask with significantly fewer tokens, especially in complex multi-hop scenarios, by avoiding high computational overhead of sequential rounds. (Page 19)

dataset_performance.label: Dataset Performance
dataset_performance.summary: Empirical results across specific multi-hop QA datasets.

fact_datasets_used.label: Evaluated Datasets
fact_datasets_used.summary: T2RAG performance was measured using the 2Wiki, HotpotQA, and MuSiQue datasets. (Page 19)

triplet_extraction_quality.label: Triplet Extraction Quality
triplet_extraction_quality.summary: Analysis of the OpenIE (Open Information Extraction) process used to convert unstructured text into structured triplets.

extraction_metrics.label: Extraction Performance Metrics
extraction_metrics.summary: Quantitative reliability scores of the OpenIE triplet extraction module based on 50 sampled documents from 2Wiki.

fact_precision_recall.label: Reliability Scores
fact_precision_recall.summary: The extraction process achieved 95.9% Precision, 98.2% Recall, and a 95.0% F1 Score. (Page 20)

fact_avg_counts.label: Extraction Density
fact_avg_counts.summary: Average extraction yields were 11.6 triplets per document and 10.5 entities per document. (Page 20)

extraction_error_types.label: IE Error Categories
extraction_error_types.summary: Classification of failures in the triplet extraction process.

err_missing.label: Missing Error
err_missing.summary: A key fact present in the text is not extracted. Occurrence rate: 52.0% of affected documents. (Page 20, 21)

err_overmerge.label: Over-merge Error
err_overmerge.summary: Two or more distinct facts are incorrectly combined into a single triplet. Occurrence rate: 40.0% of affected documents. (Page 20, 21)

err_inaccurate.label: Inaccurate Error
err_inaccurate.summary: An element of the triplet is extracted with minor errors. Occurrence rate: 10.0% of affected documents. (Page 20, 21)

err_oversplit.label: Over-split Error
err_oversplit.summary: A single cohesive fact is incorrectly split into multiple triplets. Occurrence rate: 10.0% of affected documents. (Page 20, 21)

err_placeholder.label: Placeholder Error
err_placeholder.summary: A generic and uninformative triplet is extracted. Occurrence rate: 4.0% of affected documents. (Page 20, 21)

err_hallucination.label: Extraction Hallucination
err_hallucination.summary: A triplet is generated that is not supported by the source text. Occurrence rate: 2.0% of affected documents. (Page 20, 21)

systemic_error_analysis.label: Systemic Error Analysis
systemic_error_analysis.summary: Identification of primary bottlenecks in the full pipeline based on 1000 samples from the MuSiQue dataset.

resolution_bottleneck.label: Resolution Phase Failures
resolution_bottleneck.summary: Errors occurring when the system has the correct information but fails to synthesize it.

fact_resolution_rate.label: Wrong Resolution Rate
fact_resolution_rate.summary: The most prevalent error type ('Retrieved correct but wrong resolution') accounts for 46.0% of all failure cases. (Page 20)

retrieval_bottleneck.label: Retrieval Phase Failures
retrieval_bottleneck.summary: Errors where the necessary atomic facts are not discovered.

fact_missing_retrieval_rate.label: Missing Retrieval Rate
fact_missing_retrieval_rate.summary: 'Missing retrieval' constitutes 31.2% of errors. Combined with resolution errors, these represent over 77% of all failures. (Page 20)

other_failures.label: Miscellaneous Failures
other_failures.summary: Less frequent failure modes in the T2RAG pipeline.

fact_hallucination_rate.label: Pipeline Hallucination Rate
fact_hallucination_rate.summary: General hallucination accounts for 12.7% of errors. (Page 20)

fact_incorrect_synthesis_rate.label: Synthesis Error Rate
fact_incorrect_synthesis_rate.summary: Generating an incorrect final answer despite all intermediate steps being correct accounts for 10.0% of errors. (Page 20)

rag_taxonomy.label: RAG Methodology Taxonomy
rag_taxonomy.summary: Classification of existing RAG approaches that inform the design of T2RAG.

single_round_rag.label: Single-round RAG
single_round_rag.summary: Systems that retrieve a fixed set of documents in a single pass.

fact_sparse_retrievers.label: Sparse Retrievers
fact_sparse_retrievers.summary: Classical methods like TF-IDF and BM25 paired with extractive readers. (Page 20)

fact_dense_retrievers.label: Dense Retrievers
fact_dense_retrievers.summary: Methods like DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) that use learned embeddings. (Page 20)

fact_react.label: ReAct
fact_react.summary: Interleaves chain-of-thought (CoT) steps with search actions issued by the LLM. (Page 20)

fact_query2doc.label: Query2Doc
fact_query2doc.summary: Expands queries into concise triplets to reduce token usage while maintaining recall. (Page 20)

result_side_multi_round.label: Result-Side Multi-round
result_side_multi_round.summary: Approaches that use generated intermediate results to inform the next retrieval iteration.

fact_multi_round_methods.label: Iterative Retrieval Methods
fact_multi_round_methods.summary: Includes Beam Retrieval (multiple passage hypotheses), FLARE (forecasting upcoming sentences), IRCoT/ITER-RETGEN (alternating CoT and evidence fetching), and Adaptive QA. (Page 20)

fact_graph_methods.label: Graph RAG Implementations
fact_graph_methods.summary: Includes LightRAG (dual-level retrieval), Mini-RAG (heterogeneous graph for SLMs), and HippoRAG/HippoRAG2 (synonym links and PageRank algorithm). (Page 21)

summarization_rag.label: Summarization-based RAG
summarization_rag.summary: Building hierarchical trees of summaries to capture varying levels of abstraction.

fact_sum_methods.label: Summarization Implementations
fact_sum_methods.summary: Includes Raptor (recursive clustering and summarization) and SireRAG (relatedness trees of fine-grained propositions). (Page 21)

error_distribution.label: Error Type Distribution
error_distribution.summary: Quantitative breakdown of failure modes across 775 cases (Page 22).

err_wrong_resolution.label: Retrieved Correct but Wrong Resolution
err_wrong_resolution.summary: The most frequent error type, occurring in 354 cases (46.0%) (Page 22).

err_missing_retrieval.label: Missing Retrieval
err_missing_retrieval.summary: Failure to retrieve necessary information, occurring in 240 cases (31.2%) (Page 22).

err_wrong_final_answer.label: All Correct but Wrong Final Answer
err_wrong_final_answer.summary: Failure at the final synthesis stage despite correct retrieval, occurring in 77 cases (10.0%) (Page 22).

lim_complexity.label: Complexity Constraints
lim_complexity.summary: Round methods are limited to 3 iterations to match dataset complexity and ensure fair efficiency comparison (Page 22).

lim_resources.label: Resource Constraints
lim_resources.summary: Lack of resources to test LLM-based embedding models, re-rankers, or large external KGs like Wikipedia KG (Page 22).

lim_eval.label: Evaluation Constraints
lim_eval.summary: Evaluation is limited to black-box and end-to-end analysis, which may lack explainability without recall scores of chunks (Page 22).

lim_extraction.label: Extraction Dependency
lim_extraction.summary: High dependency on triplet extraction quality; simple triplets may fail to represent complex many-to-many relationships (Page 22).

lim_scalability.label: Scalability Constraints
lim_scalability.summary: Building indices from very large corpora is token-intensive, though efficient when using pre-existing triplet databases (Page 22).

experimental_fairness.label: Experimental Fairness
experimental_fairness.summary: Methodology used to ensure fair comparison between iterative and direct retrieval baselines.

eff_topk.label: Effective Top-K
eff_topk.summary: A normalization metric defined as k * average number of iterations. Used to address 'information imbalance' by ensuring methods are compared based on total volume of retrieved information (Page 23).

edge_case_handling.label: Edge Case Handling
edge_case_handling.summary: Defined behavior for scenarios where no searchable triplets are identified.

termination_logic.label: Iteration Termination
termination_logic.summary: If query decomposition or refinement fails to generate valid triplets, the loop terminates immediately and proceeds to final answer generation using available context (Page 23).

reasoning_mechanisms.label: Reasoning Mechanisms
reasoning_mechanisms.summary: The logic and strategies used by T2RAG to resolve multi-hop queries.

structured_variable_locking.label: Structured Variable Locking
structured_variable_locking.summary: A mechanism that forces the system to continue iterating until all unbound placeholders (variables) in a decomposed query are resolved (Page 23-24).

svl_decomposition.label: Logical Decomposition
svl_decomposition.summary: Queries are broken into rigid logical constraints with placeholders (e.g., (Song, performer, ?performer) and (?performer, child, ?child)) (Page 24).

svl_resolution.label: Step-wise Resolution
svl_resolution.summary: Variables are resolved sequentially (e.g., ?performer is resolved to 'Roger Miller') (Page 24).

svl_forced_iteration.label: Forced Iteration
svl_forced_iteration.summary: Unlike agents that abandon tasks after failed retrievals (e.g., IRCoT), T2RAG continues iterating as long as a slot (like ?child) remains empty (Page 24).

system_components.label: System Components
system_components.summary: The architectural elements and prompts that drive the T2RAG process.

prompt_templates.label: Prompt Templates
prompt_templates.summary: Standardized templates used at different stages of the pipeline (Page 24).

llm_decompose.label: LLMDecompose
llm_decompose.summary: Prompt template used for structured query decomposition (Page 24).

llm_resolve.label: LLMResolve
llm_resolve.summary: Prompt template used for triplet resolving (Page 24).

llm_answer.label: LLMAnswer
llm_answer.summary: Prompt template used for final answer generation (Page 24).

t2rag_root.label: T2RAG (Triplets-to-RAG)
t2rag_root.summary: A retrieval-augmented generation system that utilizes structural triplet-based reasoning to solve multi-hop queries by shifting relational structuring to the offline phase while performing implicit graph construction during inference.

t2rag_workflow.label: Operational Workflow
t2rag_workflow.summary: The three-stage process T2RAG uses to move from a raw query to a final answer: Query Decomposition, Triplets Resolving, and Final Answering.

workflow_decomp.label: Structured Query Decomposition
workflow_decomp.summary: The initial phase where a natural language query is broken down into a series of logical reasoning steps and formal knowledge triples.

fact_decomp_format.label: Triple Format
fact_decomp_format.summary: Knowledge is extracted in the format: subject | predicate | object.

fact_decomp_placeholders.label: Placeholder Usage
fact_decomp_placeholders.summary: The symbol '?' is used as a placeholder for unknown entities that need to be resolved.

fact_decomp_comparative.label: Comparative Reasoning
fact_decomp_comparative.summary: For queries involving multiple entities, distinct placeholders (e.g., ?directorA, ?directorB) are used to maintain entity separation.

workflow_resolving.label: Triplets Resolving
workflow_resolving.summary: The iterative process of filling '?' placeholders using retrieved context passages and propositions.

fact_searchable_clues.label: Searchable Clues
fact_searchable_clues.summary: Clues containing exactly one '?' placeholder, which are resolved by replacing the placeholder with the correct entity and attributes from the context.

fact_fuzzy_clues.label: Fuzzy Clues
fact_fuzzy_clues.summary: Clues containing multiple '?' placeholders; these are handled by replacing one placeholder to create a 'Newly Searchable Clue'.

fact_resolution_process.label: Iterative Grounding
fact_resolution_process.summary: The system iteratively resolves triplets until all placeholders are filled or no further information can be retrieved from the context.

workflow_answering.label: Final Answering
workflow_answering.summary: The synthesis of resolved clues to provide a concise answer to the original query.

fact_answer_constraints.label: Answer Constraints
fact_answer_constraints.summary: Answers must be concise: WH-questions require only the exact entity/date/name; Yes/No questions require only 'yes' or 'no' without explanation.

arch_safeguards.label: Structural Safeguards
arch_safeguards.summary: Mechanisms to prevent information loss during OpenIE (Open Information Extraction) processes.

fact_fallback_mechanism.label: Text Chunk Fallback
fact_fallback_mechanism.summary: T2RAG falls back on original text chunks pre-mapped to retrieved triplets if the condensed triplet representation is insufficient (Page 25).

arch_efficiency.label: Efficiency Trade-offs
arch_efficiency.summary: The balance between offline preparation and online inference costs.

fact_offline_structuring.label: Relational Structuring
fact_offline_structuring.summary: T2RAG shifts relational structuring to the offline phase, increasing indexing cost but decreasing online inference time (Page 25).

fact_online_inference_cost.label: Inference Comparison
fact_online_inference_cost.summary: T2RAG is faster and cheaper during online inference than methods like IRCoT, which incur severe token and time costs (Page 25).

arch_embeddings.label: Performance and Embedding Quality
arch_embeddings.summary: Technical justification for using triplet embeddings over chunk embeddings.

fact_embedding_granularity.label: Triplet vs Chunk Granularity
fact_embedding_granularity.summary: Triplet embeddings isolate specific Subject-Predicate-Object relationships, reducing noise compared to chunk embeddings which average multiple facts into one vector (Page 26).

fact_faiss_efficiency.label: FAISS Integration
fact_faiss_efficiency.summary: Uses FAISS for Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) retrieval, where approximation errors are theoretically bounded (Page 26).

arch_graph_relation.label: Relation to GraphRAG
arch_graph_relation.summary: Differences in how graph structures are constructed and utilized.

fact_implicit_construction.label: Implicit Graph Construction
fact_implicit_construction.summary: Unlike explicit graph construction during indexing, T2RAG allows the LLM to construct necessary graph structures internally within its context window during the final answering stage (Page 26).

t2rag_example.label: Case Study: Film Director Comparison
t2rag_example.summary: An applied instance of T2RAG reasoning to determine which film's director was born earlier.

ex_query.label: Query
ex_query.summary: Which film has the director born earlier, 'God’s Gift To Women' or 'AldriAnnet Enn Brak'?

ex_resolution_a.label: Film A Resolution
ex_resolution_a.summary: Film: God's Gift to Women -> Director: Michael Curtiz -> Birth Year: 1886.

ex_resolution_b.label: Film B Resolution
ex_resolution_b.summary: Film: AldriAnnet Enn Brak -> Director: Edith Carlmar -> Birth Year: 1911.

ex_final_answer.label: Conclusion
ex_final_answer.summary: God’s Gift To Women (since Michael Curtiz was born in 1886, earlier than Edith Carlmar's 1911).

general_rag.label: General RAG Framework
general_rag.summary: The foundational architecture of Retrieval-Augmented Generation designed to provide accurate and contextually relevant responses.

rag_components.label: RAG Components
rag_components.summary: The two primary modules that constitute a RAG system.

generation_component.label: Generation Component
generation_component.summary: The module that leverages the LLM to produce coherent and contextually relevant responses using the retrieved information.

rag_equation.label: RAG Equation
rag_equation.summary: Defined as M = (G, R) where R = (phi, psi). The process is M(q; D) = G(q, psi(q; D_hat)) where D_hat = phi(D). (Page 1)

rag_limitations.label: Existing RAG Limitations
rag_limitations.summary: Shortcomings of traditional RAG systems that LightRAG and T2RAG aim to solve.

flat_representation_issue.label: Flat Data Representations
flat_representation_issue.summary: Traditional RAG relies on flat data, which restricts the ability to understand and retrieve information based on intricate relationships between entities. (Page 1)

contextual_awareness_gap.label: Lack of Contextual Awareness
contextual_awareness_gap.summary: Failure to maintain coherence across various entities and interrelations, leading to fragmented answers that fail to capture complex inter-dependencies. (Page 1)

lightrag.label: LightRAG
lightrag.summary: A model that integrates a graph-based text indexing paradigm with a dual-level retrieval framework to enhance coherence and contextual richness.

lightrag_indexing.label: LightRAG Text Indexing
lightrag_indexing.summary: The method of organizing text using graph structures combined with vector representations.

vector_graph_integration.label: Vector-Graph Integration
vector_graph_integration.summary: The integration of graph structures with vector representations facilitates efficient retrieval of related entities and relationships while maintaining contextual relevance. (Page 1)

dual_level_retrieval.label: Dual-Level Retrieval Framework
dual_level_retrieval.summary: A retrieval strategy that balances precise and broad information discovery.

low_level_retrieval.label: Low-Level Retrieval
low_level_retrieval.summary: Retrieval focusing on precise information regarding specific entities and their immediate relationships. (Page 1)

high_level_retrieval.label: High-Level Retrieval
high_level_retrieval.summary: Retrieval encompassing broader topics and conceptual themes. (Page 1)

incremental_update.label: Incremental Update Algorithm
incremental_update.summary: A mechanism for adding new data to the system without rebuilding the entire index.

dynamic_adaptation.label: Dynamic Data Adaptation
dynamic_adaptation.summary: Ensures timely integration of new data, allowing the system to remain effective and responsive in rapidly changing data environments. (Page 1)

t2rag.label: T2RAG
t2rag.summary: A RAG approach that leverages dynamic reasoning structures and the locality assumption to avoid rigid graph pre-processing.

t2rag_reasoning.label: Dynamic Reasoning Capabilities
t2rag_reasoning.summary: T2RAG's ability to handle complex query structures without pre-defined schemas.

reasoning_structures.label: Dynamic Reasoning Structures
reasoning_structures.summary: T2RAG can dynamically handle entity ambiguity and diverse reasoning structures including chains, trees, or Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) based on the query. (Page 27)

reasoning_model_dependency.label: Reasoning Model Leverage
reasoning_model_dependency.summary: T2RAG benefits significantly from state-of-the-art reasoning models, such as Gemini-2.5-flash, to utilize 'soft' reasoning power. (Page 27)

locality_assumption.label: Locality Assumption
locality_assumption.summary: The theory that complex offline graph construction is often unnecessary for effective retrieval.

hop_limit.label: 3-Hop Locality
hop_limit.summary: The locality assumption is particularly effective for questions within 3 hops of the source. (Page 27)

star_graph_structure.label: Text Chunk Topology
star_graph_structure.summary: In Knowledge Graphs, a text chunk typically forms a star graph or a densely connected cluster. (Page 27)

retrieval_equivalence.label: Retrieval Equivalence
retrieval_equivalence.summary: Traversing a pre-built subgraph yields a similar information set to retrieving all triplets associated with a relevant chunk. (Page 27)

t2rag_filtering.label: T2RAG Filtering Mechanism
t2rag_filtering.summary: The process of refining retrieved triplets using the LLM.

pagerank_style_filtering.label: PageRank-style Filtering
pagerank_style_filtering.summary: T2RAG aggregates triplets and uses the LLM to filter or combine them using the decomposed query, shifting the computational burden from the indexing stage to the inference stage. (Page 27)

rigid_graph_constraints.label: Rigid Graph Pre-processing
rigid_graph_constraints.summary: Methods like HippoRAG2 (Gutiérrez et al., 2025b) and RAPTOR (Sarthi et al., 2024) use 'hard' graph structures that can constrain the 'soft' reasoning power of the LLM. (Page 27)

general_architecture.label: General Architecture
general_architecture.summary: The high-level structural design of LightRAG, coordinating the flow from input query to generative response.

retrieval_module.label: Retrieval Module (R)
retrieval_module.summary: The system component responsible for indexing the external database and retrieving relevant documents based on a query.

data_indexer.label: Data Indexer φ(·)
data_indexer.summary: A function that builds a specific data structure ²Õ (indexed data) based on the external database D.

data_retriever.label: Data Retriever ψ(·)
data_retriever.summary: A function that obtains relevant documents by comparing the input query q against the indexed data structure ²Õ.

generative_model.label: Generative Model G(·)
generative_model.summary: The LLM component that produces high-quality, contextually relevant responses using the initial query q and the information retrieved via ψ(·).

performance_objectives.label: Performance Objectives
performance_objectives.summary: The key goals driving the design of the LightRAG system.

obj_comprehensive.label: Comprehensive Information Retrieval
obj_comprehensive.summary: The indexing function φ(·) must be capable of extracting global information to improve query answering effectiveness.

obj_efficient.label: Efficient and Low-Cost Retrieval
obj_efficient.summary: The data structure ²Õ must allow for rapid, cost-effective retrieval to handle high query volumes.

obj_adaptation.label: Fast Adaptation to Data Changes
obj_adaptation.summary: The system must swiftly adjust the data structure to incorporate new information from the knowledge base to remain current.

graph_text_indexing.label: Graph-Based Text Indexing
graph_text_indexing.summary: A process that transforms raw text documents into a comprehensive knowledge graph for better information understanding and retrieval.

graph_generation_formalism.label: Graph Generation Formalism
graph_generation_formalism.summary: The mathematical representation of the knowledge graph generation process.

fact_graph_formula.label: Formula: ²Õ = (²V, ²E) = Dedupe ∘ Prof(V, E), V, E = ∪ Di∈D Recog(Di)
fact_graph_formula.summary: The resulting knowledge graph ²Õ consists of nodes ²V and edges ²E, created by applying the Recog function to document chunks, followed by Profiling and Deduplication. (Page 2-3)

indexing_functions.label: Indexing Functions
indexing_functions.summary: The specific LLM-powered steps used to build the graph index.

fn_extract.label: Extracting Entities and Relationships R(·)
fn_extract.summary: Prompts an LLM to identify entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges) within text segmented into multiple chunks Di. (Page 3)

fn_profile.label: LLM Profiling P(·)
fn_profile.summary: Generates a text key-value pair (K, V) for each entity node and relation edge. Keys are short phrases for retrieval; values are summary paragraphs for generation. (Page 3)

fn_dedupe.label: Deduplication D(·)
fn_dedupe.summary: Identifies and merges identical entities and relations from different segments to reduce graph size and computational overhead. (Page 3)

indexing_advantages.label: Indexing Advantages
indexing_advantages.summary: The benefits provided by the graph-based approach over traditional methods.

adv_global_info.label: Comprehensive Information Understanding
adv_global_info.summary: Enables extraction of global information from multi-hop subgraphs, facilitating answers to complex queries spanning multiple chunks. (Page 3)

adv_performance.label: Enhanced Retrieval Performance
adv_performance.summary: Key-value structures are optimized for rapid/precise retrieval, outperforming embedding matching and chunk traversal. (Page 3)

incremental_adaptation.label: Incremental Knowledge Adaptation
incremental_adaptation.summary: The mechanism by which LightRAG updates its knowledge base without reprocessing the entire database.

adaptation_process.label: Incremental Update Algorithm
adaptation_process.summary: The technical process for adding new document D'.

fact_update_method.label: Update Method: ²Õ' = φ(D'), then ²V = ²V ∪ ²V' and ²E = ²E ∪ ²E'
fact_update_method.summary: The new document is indexed into a temporary graph ²Õ', which is then merged into the main graph via union of node and edge sets. (Page 3)

adaptation_goals.label: Adaptation Objectives
adaptation_goals.summary: The primary goals of the incremental update module.

goal_seamless.label: Seamless Integration
goal_seamless.summary: Preserves the integrity of established connections and allows new data integration without disrupting existing graph structures. (Page 3)

goal_overhead.label: Reducing Computational Overhead
goal_overhead.summary: Eliminates the need to rebuild the entire index graph, reducing resource consumption and facilitating rapid assimilation. (Page 3)

query_types.label: Query Types
query_types.summary: The two categories of user inquiries the system is designed to handle.

q_specific.label: Specific Queries
q_specific.summary: Detail-oriented queries referencing specific entities (e.g., 'Who wrote Pride and Prejudice?'). (Page 3)

q_abstract.label: Abstract Queries
q_abstract.summary: Conceptual queries encompassing broader topics, summaries, or overarching themes (e.g., 'How does AI influence modern education?'). (Page 3)

retrieval_levels.label: Retrieval Levels
retrieval_levels.summary: The two operational modes of the retriever.

level_low.label: Low-Level Retrieval
level_low.summary: Focuses on retrieving specific entities and their associated attributes or relationships. (Page 3)

level_high.label: High-Level Retrieval
level_high.summary: Aggregates information across multiple related entities and relationships to provide insights into higher-level concepts. (Page 3)

hybrid_integration.label: Graph and Vector Integration
hybrid_integration.summary: The synergy between graph structures and vector representations to optimize the search process.

step_extraction.label: Query Keyword Extraction
step_extraction.summary: The process of extracting both local query keywords k(l) and global query keywords k(g) from the input query q. (Page 4)

step_matching.label: Keyword Matching
step_matching.summary: Using a vector database to match local keywords k(l) with candidate entities and global keywords k(g) with relations linked to global keys. (Page 4)

raag.label: Retrieval-Augmented Answer Generation
raag.summary: The process of using retrieved graph-based information to generate a final answer via a Large Language Model (LLM).

info_utilization.label: Utilization of Retrieved Information
info_utilization.summary: The method of preparing retrieved data for the LLM using specific functions and data types.

profiling_function.label: Profiling Function P(·)
profiling_function.summary: A function used to produce concatenated values V from relevant entities and relations retrieved via ψ(q; ˆD).

retrieved_data_components.label: Retrieved Data Components
retrieved_data_components.summary: The specific types of information included in the concatenated values V provided to the LLM.

fact_data_types.label: Data Types in V
fact_data_types.summary: Includes entity names, relation names, descriptions of entities and relations, and excerpts from the original source text. (Section 3.3)

context_integration.label: Context Integration and Answer Generation
context_integration.summary: The final step where the LLM unifies the user query with multi-source text to create a tailored response.

generation_goal.label: Generation Goal
generation_goal.summary: To generate informative answers aligned with the query's intent by integrating both context and query into the LLM. (Section 3.3)

complexity.label: Complexity Analysis
complexity.summary: An analysis of the computational overhead associated with the indexing and retrieval phases of LightRAG.

index_phase.label: Graph-based Index Phase
index_phase.summary: The initial phase where raw text is converted into a knowledge graph of entities and relationships.

index_mechanism.label: Index Mechanism
index_mechanism.summary: The LLM is used to extract entities and relationships from each chunk of text. (Section 3.4)

index_overhead.label: Index Computational Overhead
index_overhead.summary: The LLM must be called a total of (total tokens / chunk size) times. There is no additional overhead for updates to new text. (Section 3.4)

retrieval_phase.label: Graph-based Retrieval Phase

kg_prelims.label: Knowledge Graph (KG) Preliminaries
kg_prelims.summary: The fundamental mathematical representation of a knowledge graph used in the ReKnoS framework.

kg_triple_definition.label: KG Triple Definition
kg_triple_definition.summary: A KG is defined as G = {⟨e, r, e′⟩ | e, e′ ∈ E, r ∈ R}, where E is the set of entities and R is the set of relations. Each triple captures a factual relationship from a head entity e to a tail entity e′ via relation r. (Page 3)

super_relations_concept.label: Super-Relations
super_relations_concept.summary: An abstraction layer that groups multiple granular, detailed relations into a single higher-level representative relation to reduce computational complexity and LLM query overhead.

super_rel_formal_def.label: Formal Definition of Super-Relation
super_rel_formal_def.summary: A super-relation R is defined as a group of more granular, detailed relations R = {r1, r2, ..., rn}, where each ri is a specific relation on the KG. Example: 'music.featured_artist' as R encompasses {'music.featured_artist.recordings', 'music.featured_artist.albums', ...}. (Page 3)

super_rel_implementation.label: Super-Relation Implementation
super_rel_implementation.summary: In Wikidata, super-relations are derived from the second level of a three-level hierarchy (e.g., music -> featured_artist -> recordings). In KGs without inherent hierarchy, they are created by clustering relations based on semantic similarity and using textually coherent cluster centers. (Page 3)

super_rel_purpose.label: Purpose of Super-Relations
super_rel_purpose.summary: To efficiently gather information from granular relations and reduce the complexity of handling numerous fine-grained relations while preserving relevant reasoning information. (Page 3)

super_relation_paths.label: Super-Relation Search Paths
super_relation_paths.summary: The formal structure of how the framework traverses the KG using super-relations.

super_rel_connection_def.label: Definition 1: Super-Relation Connection
super_rel_connection_def.summary: R1 connects to R2 (R1 -> R2) iff there exist entities e1, e2, and e3 such that e1 --r1--> e2 and e2 --r2--> e3, where r1 ∈ R1 and r2 ∈ R2. (Page 3)

super_rel_path_def.label: Definition 2: Super-Relation Path
super_rel_path_def.summary: A super-relation path P = (R1 -> R2 -> ... -> Rl) of length l consists of l consecutively connected super-relations. (Page 3)

super_rel_search_path_def.label: Definition 3: Super-Relation Search Path
super_rel_search_path_def.summary: A search path Ql of length l consists of l super-relation sets Ql = {S1, S2, ..., Sl}, where Si = {R(1), ..., R(|Si|)}. For every R in Si, there must exist at least one R' in Si+1 such that R -> R' for i = 1, ..., l-1. (Page 3)

reknos_reasoning_process.label: ReKnoS Reasoning Process
reknos_reasoning_process.summary: The iterative algorithmic process used to traverse the KG and retrieve an answer.

reasoning_steps_logic.label: Reasoning Step Logic
reasoning_steps_logic.summary: The framework performs up to L reasoning steps. At each step l, it aims to select a set Sl of N important super-relations. After each step, the LLM decides whether to extract the answer from retrieved entities or proceed to step l+1. (Page 4)

candidate_selection_process.label: Candidate Selection
candidate_selection_process.summary: The set of candidate super-relations Cl for step l is defined as Cl = {R | ∃R' ∈ Sl-1 such that R' -> R}. This collects all super-relations directly connected to the previous set Sl-1. (Page 4)

scoring_mechanism.label: Scoring and Filtering
scoring_mechanism.summary: If the number of candidates M = |Cl| exceeds the target size N, an LLM assigns a score {s1, ..., sM} to each candidate. The N super-relations with the highest scores are selected to form Sl. (Page 4)

super_relation_selection.label: Super-Relation Selection Process
super_relation_selection.summary: The process of using an LLM to identify and score the most relevant super-relations to guide the reasoning path.

llm_prompting_mechanism.label: LLM Prompting Mechanism
llm_prompting_mechanism.summary: The method of requesting the LLM to select the most helpful relations for answering a query.

prompt_structure_fact.label: Prompt Structure
prompt_structure_fact.summary: The prompt includes the Question, Topic Entity, and Candidate Relations, requesting the LLM to select N (e.g., N=3) relations. (Page 5)

complexity_reduction_fact.label: Complexity Reduction
complexity_reduction_fact.summary: Super-relations are not explicitly informed to the LLM in the prompt to reduce unnecessary complexity. (Page 5)

scoring_and_ranking.label: Scoring and Ranking
scoring_and_ranking.summary: The process of ranking super-relations based on LLM-assigned scores to select the top N candidates.

score_sorting_fact.label: Score Sorting
score_sorting_fact.summary: Scores are sorted in descending order: s(1)_l >= s(2)_l >= ... >= s(M)_l, where s(i)_l is the i-th largest score. (Page 5)

selected_set_fact.label: Selected Super-Relation Set
selected_set_fact.summary: The set Sl contains the N super-relations with the highest scores: Sl = {R(1)_l, R(2)_l, ..., R(N)_l}. (Page 5)

score_normalization.label: Score Normalization
score_normalization.summary: Normalizing the scores of selected super-relations to ensure they sum to 1 for scaled influence in subsequent iterations.

normalization_formula_fact.label: Normalization Formula
normalization_formula_fact.summary: s(k)_l = s(k)_l / sum_{j=1 to N}(s(j)_l) for k = 1, ..., N. (Page 5)

super_relation_path_selection.label: Super-Relation Path Selection
super_relation_path_selection.summary: The identification of the most relevant paths of super-relations from the retrieved search path Ql.

path_representation.label: Super-Relation Path Representation
path_representation.summary: A super-relation path Pi is a sequence of super-relations from length 1 to l.

path_formula_fact.label: Path Formula
path_formula_fact.summary: Pi = R(ki,1)_1 -> R(ki,2)_2 -> ... -> R(ki,l)_l, where ki,j is the index of the super-relation in the j-th position. (Page 6)

theorem_4_1.label: Theorem 4.1: Path Existence
theorem_4_1.summary: A super-relation search path Ql leads to at least one super-relation path P of length l. (Page 6)

path_scoring_mechanism.label: Path Scoring Mechanism
path_scoring_mechanism.summary: Calculating the total score of a path to select the K most relevant paths (P*).

top_k_selection_fact.label: Top-K Selection
top_k_selection_fact.summary: P* = arg max Score(P) such that |Pf| <= K. (Page 6)

entity_extraction_selection.label: Score-Based Entity Extraction Selection
entity_extraction_selection.summary: The process of extracting entities at the end of the selected super-relation paths to determine if the query can be answered.

theorem_4_2.label: Theorem 4.2: KG Reasoning Path Existence
theorem_4_2.summary: For any super-relation path P, there exists at least one corresponding KG reasoning path (relation path) of length l where ri is a relation chosen from super-relation R(ki). (Page 6)

final_entity_set.label: Final Entity Set E(kl)
final_entity_set.summary: The set of all entities that satisfy the connection property of the super-relation path P.

entity_set_formula_fact.label: Entity Set Formula
entity_set_formula_fact.summary: E(kl) = {e | exists r1 in R(k1)_1, ..., rl in R(kl)_l, such that e1 r1-> e2 r2-> ... rl-> e}. (Page 6)

llm_decision_loop.label: LLM Decision Loop
llm_decision_loop.summary: The iterative process where the LLM decides whether the retrieved entities are sufficient to answer the query or if the search path length l should be increased.

termination_condition_fact.label: Termination Condition
termination_condition_fact.summary: The process terminates and the LLM is asked for the final answer if the LLM deems entities sufficient OR if l = L. (Page 6)

iteration_fact.label: Path Extension
iteration_fact.summary: If entities are insufficient, the process repeats from Section 4.1, increasing path length to l + 1. (Page 6)

prompting_baselines_fact.label: Prompting Baselines
prompting_baselines_fact.summary: Includes standard prompting (IO prompt), Chain-of-Thought (CoT), and Self-Consistency. (Page 7)

hits_at_1_fact.label: Hits@1
hits_at_1_fact.summary: The primary metric used for reporting results across various datasets using GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini. (Page 7)

fact_complex_dataset_perf.summary: ReKnoS outperforms baselines in complex datasets; e.g., GrailQA accuracy: 71.9% (GPT-3.5) and 80.5% (GPT-4o-mini) vs KG-Agent's 68.9% and 77.5% (p. 8).

fact_small_model_gain.summary: ReKnoS shows more significant improvement over ToG on smaller models (e.g., Llama-2-7B) compared to large models, making it more practical for deployment (p. 9).

fact_super_rel_benefit.label: Super-Relation Benefit
fact_super_rel_benefit.summary: Super-relations increase the search space size, allowing the model to encounter more fact triples and increasing the likelihood of retrieving the correct answer (p. 9).

search_space_analysis.label: Search Space Analysis
search_space_analysis.summary: Comparison of the number of fact triples encountered during search.

fact_search_space_growth.label: Search Space Growth
fact_search_space_growth.summary: On GrailQA (GPT-3.5), ReKnoS search space is 42% larger than KG-Agent and 55% larger than ToG (p. 9).

llm_call_complexity.label: LLM Call Complexity
llm_call_complexity.summary: Mathematical representation of the number of LLM calls required per question.

fact_reknoS_call_formula.label: ReKnoS Call Formula
fact_reknoS_call_formula.summary: LLM calls = (2L* + 1), where L* is the final number of reasoning steps. Calls are independent of search width N (p. 9).

fact_tog_call_formula.label: ToG Call Formula
fact_tog_call_formula.summary: LLM calls are upper bounded by (2LN + 1), making ToG's cost dependent on search width N (p. 9).

hyperparameter_analysis.summary: Investigation into how the search width (N) and search length (L) affect performance.

fact_L_N_impact.label: Impact of L and N
fact_L_N_impact.summary: Increasing both search length (L) and search width (N) leads to better performance (p. 9).

fact_N_criticality.label: Criticality of Search Width (N)
fact_N_criticality.summary: Decreasing N from 3 to 1 causes a substantial drop in Hits@1 (e.g., from 81.1% to 76.2% when L=3) (p. 9).

fact_path_capacity.label: Path Capacity
fact_path_capacity.summary: The super-relation search path Q can contain up to N^L super-relations (p. 9).

path_exploration.summary: The mechanism used to navigate multiple relations within a knowledge graph to find valid reasoning chains.

def_super_rel.label: Super-Relation Definitions
def_super_rel.summary: The fundamental building blocks of the ReKnoS reasoning process.

fact_def_1.label: Definition 1: Super-Relation Composition
fact_def_1.summary: A super-relation Ri is defined as a set of multiple standard binary relations {r1, r2, ...} that exist between entities in the knowledge graph.

fact_def_2.label: Definition 2: Super-Relation Path
fact_def_2.summary: A super-relation path P consists of l consecutive super-relations that are connected.

fact_def_3.label: Definition 3: Super-Relation Search Path
fact_def_3.summary: A super-relation search path Ql = {S1, S2, ..., Sl} consists of l super-relation sets, where each set Si contains multiple super-relations. Connectivity is guaranteed if for all R in Si, there exists R' in Si+1 such that R -> R'.

th_4_1.label: Theorem 4.1: Search Path to Super-Relation Path
th_4_1.summary: Proof that a selected super-relation search path leads to at least one valid super-relation path.

fact_th_4_1_statement.label: Theorem 4.1 Statement
fact_th_4_1_statement.summary: Given a super-relation search path of length l, Ql = {S1, S2, ..., Sl}, there exists at least one super-relation path P = R(k1) -> R(k2) -> ... -> R(kl) where R(kj) is an element of Sj.

fact_th_4_1_proof.label: Theorem 4.1 Proof Logic
fact_th_4_1_proof.summary: Proven via induction: Base case establishes connectivity between S1 and S2; inductive hypothesis assumes path exists for l-1, and Definition 3 ensures the existence of a connected super-relation R(kl) in Sl to extend the path to length l.

th_4_2.label: Theorem 4.2: Super-Relation Path to KG Reasoning Path
th_4_2.summary: Proof that any super-relation path corresponds to at least one concrete KG reasoning path.

fact_th_4_2_statement.label: Theorem 4.2 Statement
fact_th_4_2_statement.summary: For any super-relation path P = R(k1) -> R(k2) -> ... -> R(kl), there exists at least one KG reasoning path e1 -> r1 -> e2 -> r2 -> ... -> rl -> el+1, where each relation ri is chosen from the super-relation R(ki).

fact_th_4_2_proof.label: Theorem 4.2 Proof Logic
fact_th_4_2_proof.summary: Proven via induction: Base case (l=1) maps a single super-relation to a relation and two entities. Inductive step uses Definition 1 to show that the connection between R(kl-1) and R(kl) implies the existence of entities el and el+1 and a relation rl in R(kl) such that the path extends from el to el+1.

sub_super_relations.summary: The use of high-level relations to guide KG traversal.

fact_super_rel_dynamic.summary: ReKnoS is effective even without predefined super-relations by deriving them dynamically via clustering. (Page 18)

fact_halluc_filter.summary: The candidate selection step explicitly filters super-relations to include only those directly connected to previously selected relations in the KG. (Page 19)

fact_halluc_ranking.label: Grounded Ranking
fact_halluc_ranking.summary: The LLM ranks candidates that are already pre-selected based on KG existence; any hallucinated suggestions are naturally excluded from the pipeline. (Page 19)
